5.14.148.d: विपरिक्रामन्त्य् एत ऋत्विजस् । विपरिहरन्ति हवीँषि दक्षिणतः पुरोडाशम् आसादयति ।

5.14.149.s: uttarataḥ karambham āśaya eva dhānā bhavanti
5.14.149.d: उत्तरतः करम्भम् आशय एव धाना भवन्ति
5.14.149.m:
the groats to the north;
the parched grains remain in the receptacle itself.

5.14.149.s: dakṣiṇata upaviśato brahmā ca yajamānaś cottarato 'dhvaryuś cāgnīdhraś ca |
5.14.149.d: दक्षिणत उपविशतो ब्रह्मा च यजमानश् चोत्तरतो ऽध्वर्युश् चाग्नीध्रश् च ।
5.14.149.m: The brahman and the sacrificer sit to the south, and the adhvaryu priest and the āgnīdhra priest sit to the north.
Then, having cut off the prāśitra portion, he cuts off the iḍā.

5.15.149.s: upahūtāyām iḍāyām agnīdha ādadhāti ṣaḍavattam | nighreṇa bhakṣayitvā barhiṣi saṃnyasyanti |
5.15.149.d: उपहूतायाम् इडायाम् अग्नीध आदधाति षडवत्तम् । निघ्रेण भक्षयित्वा बर्हिषि संन्यस्यन्ति ।
5.15.149.m:
When the iḍā has been invoked, he gives the six-cut portion to the āgnīdhra priest;
having consumed [their portions] by smelling, they deposit them on the barhis.

5.15.149.s: atha prācīnāvītāni kṛtvā puroḍāśaṃ dhānāḥ karambham iti pātryām̐ saṃprayauti
5.15.149.d: अथ प्राचीनावीतानि कृत्वा पुरोडाशं धानाः करम्भम् इति पात्र्याँ संप्रयौति
5.15.149.m: Then, having worn their sacred threads over the right shoulder, he mixes together the puroḍāśa, the parched grains, and the groats in a pan.

5.15.149.s: tisṛṣu sraktiṣu parṇaseveṣu trīn piṇḍān dadāti |
5.15.149.d: तिसृषु स्रक्तिषु पर्णसेवेषु त्रीन् पिण्डान् ददाति ।
5.15.149.m: At the three corners, on leaf-cups, he places three balls:

5.15.149.s: etat te tatāsau ye ca tvām anu | iti dakṣiṇasyām̐ śroṇyām
5.15.149.d: एतत् ते ततासौ ये च त्वाम् अनु । इति दक्षिणस्याँ श्रोण्याम्
5.15.149.m: "This for you, father, N.N., and for those who follow you," on the southern hip;

5.15.149.s: etat te pitāmahāsau ye ca tvām anu | iti dakṣiṇe 'm̐se |
5.15.149.d: एतत् ते पितामहासौ ये च त्वाम् अनु । इति दक्षिणे ऽँसे ।
5.15.149.m: "This for you, grandfather, N.N., and for those who follow you," on the southern shoulder;

5.15.149.s: etat te prapitāmahāsau ye ca tvām anu | ity uttare 'm̐se |
5.15.149.d: एतत् ते प्रपितामहासौ ये च त्वाम् अनु । इत्य् उत्तरे ऽँसे ।
5.15.149.m: "This for you, great-grandfather, N.N., and for those who follow you," on the northern shoulder.

5.15.149.s: uttarasyām̐ śroṇyāṃ lepaṃ nimārṣṭi | eṣā yuṣmākam iyam asmākam imāṃ vayaṃ jīvā jīvanto 'nusaṃcaranto bhūyāsma | iti |
5.15.149.d: उत्तरस्याँ श्रोण्यां लेपं निमार्ष्टि । एषा युष्माकम् इयम् अस्माकम् इमां वयं जीवा जीवन्तो ऽनुसंचरन्तो भूयास्म । इति ।
5.15.149.m: On the northern hip he wipes off the wiping [remnants], with: "This is yours; this is ours; may we, living, continue living and wandering along this [earth]!"

5.15.149.s: atra pitaro yathābhāgaṃ mandadhvam ity uktvodañco niṣkramya yajñopavītāni kṛtvāhavanīyam upatiṣṭhante susaṃdṛśaṃ tvā vayaṃ maghavan mandiṣīmahi | pra nūnaṃ pūrṇavandhura stuto yāsi vaśām̐ anu | yojā nv indra te harom iti |
5.15.149.d: अत्र पितरो यथाभागं मन्दध्वम् इत्य् उक्त्वोदञ्चो निष्क्रम्य यज्ञोपवीतानि कृत्वाहवनीयम् उपतिष्ठन्ते सुसंदृशं त्वा वयं मघवन् मन्दिषीमहि । प्र नूनं पूर्णवन्धुर स्तुतो यासि वशाँ अनु । योजा न्व् इन्द्र ते हरोम् इति ।
5.15.149.m: Having said: "Here, O Fathers, rejoice according to your share," having gone out toward the north, and having worn their sacred threads over the left shoulder, they attend upon the āhavanīya fire with: "May we rejoice in seeing you well, O generous one! / Duly praised now, having a full seat, go to your desires! / Yoke your two bay steeds now, O Indra!"

5.15.149.s: ā tamitor upatiṣṭhante | atha gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhante | akṣann amīmadanta hi | ava priyā adhūṣata | astoṣata svabhānavas | viprā naviṣṭhayā matī | yojā nv indra te harom iti |
5.15.149.d: आ तमितोर् उपतिष्ठन्ते । अथ गार्हपत्यम् उपतिष्ठन्ते । अक्षन्न् अमीमदन्त हि । अव प्रिया अधूषत । अस्तोषत स्वभानवस् । विप्रा नविष्ठया मती । योजा न्व् इन्द्र ते हरोम् इति ।
5.15.149.m:
They attend until they hold their breath.
Then they attend upon the gārhapatya fire with: "For they have eaten, they have rejoiced; / the dear ones have shaken off [distress]; / the self-radiant poets have been praised / with the newest hymn of praise; / yoke your two bay steeds now, O Indra!"

5.15.150.m: They attend until they hold their breath.

5.15.150.s: atha prācīnāvītāni kṛtvānvāhāryapacanam abhiprapadyante | akṣan pitaras | amīmadanta pitaras | atītṛpanta pitaras | amīmṛjanta pitaraḥ | pareta pitaraḥ somyās | iti |
5.15.150.d: अथ प्राचीनावीतानि कृत्वान्वाहार्यपचनम् अभिप्रपद्यन्ते । अक्षन् पितरस् । अमीमदन्त पितरस् । अतीतृपन्त पितरस् । अमीमृजन्त पितरः । परेत पितरः सोम्यास् । इति ।
5.15.150.m: Then, having worn their sacred threads over the right shoulder, they approach the anvāhāryapacana fire with: "The Fathers have eaten; / the Fathers have rejoiced; / the Fathers have been satiated; / the Fathers have cleansed themselves; / depart, O soma-loving Fathers!"

5.15.150.s: ā tamitor upatiṣṭhante sa yo balavām̐s tam āha | anenodakumbhena saṃtatayā dhārayā trir apasalaiḥ pariṣiñcan parīhi | iti
5.15.150.d: आ तमितोर् उपतिष्ठन्ते स यो बलवाँस् तम् आह । अनेनोदकुम्भेन संततया धारया त्रिर् अपसलैः परिषिञ्चन् परीहि । इति
5.15.150.m:
They attend until they hold their breath.
He says to whichever [man] is strong: "Go around three times counter-clockwise, sprinkling with a continuous stream from this water-jar."

5.15.150.s: sa tathā karoti nidhāya kumbhaṃ yathetaṃ triḥ punaḥ pratiparyeti |
5.15.150.d: स तथा करोति निधाय कुम्भं यथेतं त्रिः पुनः प्रतिपर्येति ।
5.15.150.m:
He does so;
having set down the jar, he goes around three times in reverse, just as he had come.

5.15.150.s: āharaṇaprītyeva kaśipūpabarhaṇe āñjanābhyañjane dadāti | atha vāsām̐si dadāti |
5.15.150.d: आहरणप्रीत्येव कशिपूपबर्हणे आञ्जनाभ्यञ्जने ददाति । अथ वासाँसि ददाति ।
5.15.150.m:
As if pleasing by bringing [presents], he gives a mat and a pillow, collyrium and ointment;
then he gives garments.

Then he attends with six obeisances alternately;
then he prays for a hero [son].

5.15.150.s: athainānutthāpya pravāhya tisṛbhirmana āhvayate mano nvāhuvāmaha ā na etu manaḥ punaḥ punarnaḥ pitaro mana iti |
5.15.150.d: अथैनानुत्थाप्य प्रवाह्य तिसृभिर्मन आह्वयते मनो न्वाहुवामह आ न एतु मनः पुनः पुनर्नः पितरो मन इति ।
5.15.150.m: Then, having raised them up and dispatched them, he summons the mind with three [verses]: "The mind we now summon...", "May the mind come back to us...", [and] "May the Fathers [give] us back the mind..."
At this point he throws these balls together with the leaf-cups into the fire.

5.15.150.s: atha yajñopavītāni kurvate | atha saṃpraiṣam āha brahman prasthāsyāmaḥ samidham ādhāyāgnīd agnīn sakṛtsakṛt saṃmṛḍḍhi | iti |
5.15.150.d: अथ यज्ञोपवीतानि कुर्वते । अथ संप्रैषम् आह ब्रह्मन् प्रस्थास्यामः समिधम् आधायाग्नीद् अग्नीन् सकृत्सकृत् संमृड्ढि । इति ।
5.15.150.m: Then they adjust their sacred threads over the left shoulder. Then he gives the command: "O brahman, we shall set out; O āgnīdh, having placed the kindling stick, wipe the fires once each."

5.15.150.s: atha juhūpabhṛtāv ādāyātyākramyāśrāvyāha devau yaja | iti
5.15.150.d: अथ जुहूपभृताव् आदायात्याक्रम्याश्राव्याह देवौ यज । इति
5.15.150.m: Then, taking the juhū and upabhṛt ladles, stepping across, and making the call, he says: "Recite the offering-verse for the two gods."

5.15.150.s: yaja yaja | ity apabarhiṣau dvāv anūyājāv iṣṭvodaṅṅ atyākramya yathāyatanam̐ srucau sādayitvā vājavatībhyām̐ srucau vyūhati
5.15.150.d: यज यज । इत्य् अपबर्हिषौ द्वाव् अनूयाजाव् इष्ट्वोदङ्ङ् अत्याक्रम्य यथायतनँ स्रुचौ सादयित्वा वाजवतीभ्याँ स्रुचौ व्यूहति
5.15.150.m: Having offered the two after-offerings without the barhis with "Recite the offering-verse, recite the offering-verse," stepping across to the north, and placing the two ladles in their proper places, he separates the two ladles with the two vājavatī verses.

5.15.150.s: śaṃyunā prastaraparidhi saṃprakīrya saṃprasrāvya srucau vimucyātraiva samiṣṭayajur juhoti |
5.15.150.d: शंयुना प्रस्तरपरिधि संप्रकीर्य संप्रस्राव्य स्रुचौ विमुच्यात्रैव समिष्टयजुर् जुहोति ।
5.15.150.m: Having strewed the grass bundle and the enclosing sticks together with the śaṃyu formula, and having made the ladles flow together, having unyoked [the ladles], right there he offers the samiṣṭayajus offering.

5.15.151.s: athaiteṣām̐ śastrāṇāṃ dvedve udāharanti | atha yajñopavītāni kṛtvā prājāpatyayarcā gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhante prajāpate na tvad etāny anyas | iti |
5.15.151.d: अथैतेषाँ शस्त्राणां द्वेद्वे उदाहरन्ति । अथ यज्ञोपवीतानि कृत्वा प्राजापत्ययर्चा गार्हपत्यम् उपतिष्ठन्ते प्रजापते न त्वद् एतान्य् अन्यस् । इति ।
5.15.151.m: Then they cite two [verses] each for these recitations. Then, having arranged their sacred cords over their left shoulders, they revere the gārhapatya fire with the verse addressed to Prajāpati: "O Prajāpati, no other than you..."

5.15.151.s: atraitāṃ dvitīyāṃ japati yad antarikṣaṃ pṛthivīm uta dyām iti
5.15.151.d: अत्रैतां द्वितीयां जपति यद् अन्तरिक्षं पृथिवीम् उत द्याम् इति
5.15.151.m: Here he mutters this second [verse]: "Whatever intermediate space, earth, and sky..."

5.16.151.s: yāvad evātrādhvaryuś ceṣṭati tāvad eṣa pratiprasthātā pratipūruṣaṃ traiyambakān ekakapālān ekātiriktān gārhapatye śrapayitvānabhighāritān udvāsya sate vā śrāve vā jaratkośabile vā samupyopāste |
5.16.151.d: यावद् एवात्राध्वर्युश् चेष्टति तावद् एष प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रतिपूरुषं त्रैयम्बकान् एककपालान् एकातिरिक्तान् गार्हपत्ये श्रपयित्वानभिघारितान् उद्वास्य सते वा श्रावे वा जरत्कोशबिले वा समुप्योपास्ते ।
5.16.151.m: While the adhvaryu priest is engaged here, the pratiprasthātṛ priest, having baked on the gārhapatya fire the Traiyambaka cakes on one potsherd—one for each person, plus one extra—takes them off the fire without basting them with ghee, empties them into a winnowing basket, a shallow dish, or an old broken pot-mouth, and sits waiting.

5.16.151.s: atha yācati nīlalohite sūtre antamaṃ parṇam antam āgārād ekolmukam udapātram iti |
5.16.151.d: अथ याचति नीललोहिते सूत्रे अन्तमं पर्णम् अन्तम् आगाराद् एकोल्मुकम् उदपात्रम् इति ।
5.16.151.m: Then he asks for two threads of blue and red, the topmost leaf, and a single firebrand from the innermost part of the house, and a water-pot.

5.16.151.s: etat samādāya gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhante yāvanto gṛhyā smas tebhyaḥ kam akaram | paśūnām̐ śarmāsi śarma yajamānasya śarma me yaccha | iti |
5.16.151.d: एतत् समादाय गार्हपत्यम् उपतिष्ठन्ते यावन्तो गृह्या स्मस् तेभ्यः कम् अकरम् । पशूनाँ शर्मासि शर्म यजमानस्य शर्म मे यच्छ । इति ।
5.16.151.m: Taking these, they revere the gārhapatya fire: "As many as we are of the household, for them I have brought pleasure." / "You are the protection of the animals; protection for the sacrificer, grant me protection!"

5.16.151.s: athodañco niṣkramya tāṃ diśaṃ yanti yatrāsya nityasaṃpannaścatuṣpatha spaṣṭo bhavati
5.16.151.d: अथोदञ्चो निष्क्रम्य तां दिशं यन्ति यत्रास्य नित्यसंपन्नश्चतुष्पथ स्पष्टो भवति
5.16.151.m: Then, going out towards the north, they go in that direction where an established crossroads is clearly visible to him.

5.16.151.s: yadyu vai na bhavatyanasā vā rathena vā viyānti
5.16.151.d: यद्यु वै न भवत्यनसा वा रथेन वा वियान्ति
5.16.151.m: If indeed there is none, they drive apart either with a cart or with a chariot.

5.16.151.s: tad etad ekolmukam upasamādhāya saṃparistīryāntame parṇe sarveṣāṃ traiyambakāṇām̐ sakṛtsakṛt samavadāya juhoti | eka eva rudro na dvitīyāya tasthe | ākhus te rudra paśus taṃ juṣasva | eṣa te rudra bhāgaḥ saha svasrāmbikayā taṃ juṣasva bheṣajaṃ gave 'śvāya puruṣāya bheṣajam atho asmabhyaṃ bheṣajam̐ subheṣajaṃ yathāsati sugam meṣāya meṣyai | avāmba rudram adimahy ava devaṃ tryambakam | yathā naḥ śreyasaḥ karad yathā no vasyasaḥ karad yathā naḥ paśumataḥ karad yathā no vyavasāyayāt svāhā | iti |
5.16.151.d: तद् एतद् एकोल्मुकम् उपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्यान्तमे पर्णे सर्वेषां त्रैयम्बकाणाँ सकृत्सकृत् समवदाय जुहोति । एक एव रुद्रो न द्वितीयाय तस्थे । आखुस् ते रुद्र पशुस् तं जुषस्व । एष ते रुद्र भागः सह स्वस्राम्बिकया तं जुषस्व भेषजं गवे ऽश्वाय पुरुषाय भेषजम् अथो अस्मभ्यं भेषजँ सुभेषजं यथासति सुगम् मेषाय मेष्यै । अवाम्ब रुद्रम् अदिमह्य् अव देवं त्र्यम्बकम् । यथा नः श्रेयसः करद् यथा नो वस्यसः करद् यथा नः पशुमतः करद् यथा नो व्यवसाययात् स्वाहा । इति ।
5.16.151.m: Having set down this single firebrand there and strewn around it, having cut off once from each of all the Traiyambaka cakes upon the topmost leaf, he offers: "Rudra is one only; he has not stood for a second." / "The mole-rat is your beast, O Rudra; enjoy it." / "This is your share, O Rudra, together with your sister Ambikā; enjoy it." / "Medicine for the cow, for the horse, medicine for the man, and also medicine for us, very good medicine, so that there may be ease for the ram and for the ewe." / "We have propitiated Rudra, O mother, we have propitiated god Tryambaka, / so that he may make us better off, make us wealthier, make us rich in cattle, and set us to thrive, svāhā!"

5.16.151.s: atraitad antamaṃ parṇaṃ yaṃ dveṣṭi tasya saṃcare paśūnāṃ nyasyati
5.16.151.d: अत्रैतद् अन्तमं पर्णं यं द्वेष्टि तस्य संचरे पशूनां न्यस्यति
5.16.151.m: Here, he throws this topmost leaf on the path of the cattle belonging to him whom he hates.

5.16.152.s: yady u vai na dveṣṭy ākhvavaṭe nyasyati | athaiteṣāṃ traiyambakāṇām ekaikaṃ vyutprayacchati dvau yajamānāya |
5.16.152.d: यद्य् उ वै न द्वेष्ट्य् आख्ववटे न्यस्यति । अथैतेषां त्रैयम्बकाणाम् एकैकं व्युत्प्रयच्छति द्वौ यजमानाय ।
5.16.152.m: If indeed he hates no one, he throws it into a mole-rat hole. Then he hands over these Traiyambaka cakes, one to each [person], and two to the sacrificer.

5.16.152.s: athaitam agniṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ pariyanti dakṣiṇān ūrūn upāghnānās tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam | urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt | iti
5.16.152.d: अथैतम् अग्निं त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं परियन्ति दक्षिणान् ऊरून् उपाघ्नानास् त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् । उर्वारुकम् इव बन्धनान् मृत्योर् मुक्षीय मामृतात् । इति
5.16.152.m: Then they walk clockwise three times around this fire, slapping their right thighs: "We sacrifice to Tryambaka, the fragrant increaser of prosperity; / like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be freed from death, not from immortality!"

5.16.152.s: sakṛtparītyottaratas tiṣṭhanti | utkhidanti bhagāya tvā | iti lipsantas |
5.16.152.d: सकृत्परीत्योत्तरतस् तिष्ठन्ति । उत्खिदन्ति भगाय त्वा । इति लिप्सन्तस् ।
5.16.152.m: Having walked around once, they stand to the north. They toss [the cakes] up, desiring to catch them, with: "For good fortune, thee!"

5.16.152.s: evam eva dvitīyaṃ pariyanti | evaṃ tṛtīyam athaiṣā patikāmā trir apasalaiḥ paryeti savyam ūrum upāghnānā tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ pativedanam | urvārukam iva bandhanādito mukṣīya mā pates | iti
5.16.152.d: एवम् एव द्वितीयं परियन्ति । एवं तृतीयम् अथैषा पतिकामा त्रिर् अपसलैः पर्येति सव्यम् ऊरुम् उपाघ्नाना त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पतिवेदनम् । उर्वारुकम् इव बन्धनादितो मुक्षीय मा पतेस् । इति
5.16.152.m: In the very same way they walk around a second time; in the same way a third time. Then this maiden desirous of a husband walks around counter-clockwise three times, slapping her left thigh: "We sacrifice to Tryambaka, the fragrant finder of a husband; / like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be freed from here, not from a husband!"

5.16.152.s: sakṛtparītyottartas tiṣṭhati | utkhidati bhagāya tvā | iti lipsate |
5.16.152.d: सकृत्परीत्योत्तर्तस् तिष्ठति । उत्खिदति भगाय त्वा । इति लिप्सते ।
5.16.152.m: Having walked around once, she stands to the north. She tosses [the cakes] up, desiring to catch them, with: "For good fortune, thee!"

5.16.152.s: evam eva dvitīyaṃ paryeti | evaṃ tṛtīyam athainān yajamānasyāñjalāv āvapati ||
5.16.152.d: एवम् एव द्वितीयं पर्येति । एवं तृतीयम् अथैनान् यजमानस्याञ्जलाव् आवपति ॥
5.16.152.m: In the very same way she walks around a second time; in the same way a third time. Then he pours them into the folded hands of the sacrificer.

5.17.152.s: prajayā tvā sam̐sṛjāmi māsareṇa surām iva | iti tān yajamānaḥ patnyañjalāv āvapati prajayā tvā paśubhiḥ sam̐sṛjāmi māsareṇa surām iva | iti
5.17.152.d: प्रजया त्वा सँसृजामि मासरेण सुराम् इव । इति तान् यजमानः पत्न्यञ्जलाव् आवपति प्रजया त्वा पशुभिः सँसृजामि मासरेण सुराम् इव । इति
5.17.152.m: With "I unite you with offspring as surā with māsara," the sacrificer pours them into the folded hands of the wife, with "I unite you with offspring and cattle as surā with māsara."

5.17.152.s: tān patnī duhitre bhagakāmāyai bhagena tvā sam̐sṛjāmi māsareṇa surām iva | iti |
5.17.152.d: तान् पत्नी दुहित्रे भगकामायै भगेन त्वा सँसृजामि मासरेण सुराम् इव । इति ।
5.17.152.m: The wife [pours] them to her daughter desirous of good fortune, with "I unite you with good fortune as surā with māsara."

5.17.153.s: athainān mūta opya nīlalohitābhyām̐ sūtrābhyāṃ vigrathya śuṣke vā sthāṇau viśākhāyāṃ vā badhnāti | eṣa te rudra bhāgas taṃ juṣasva tenāvasena paro mūjavato 'tīhi | avatatadhanvā pinākahastaḥ kṛttivāsom iti |
5.17.153.d: अथैनान् मूत ओप्य नीललोहिताभ्याँ सूत्राभ्यां विग्रथ्य शुष्के वा स्थाणौ विशाखायां वा बध्नाति । एष ते रुद्र भागस् तं जुषस्व तेनावसेन परो मूजवतो ऽतीहि । अवततधन्वा पिनाकहस्तः कृत्तिवासोम् इति ।
5.17.153.m: Then, having poured them into a woven basket and tied it with the blue and red threads, he binds it either to a dry tree-stump or to a fork in a branch: "This is your share, O Rudra; / enjoy it; with this provision go beyond the Mūjavat mountains!" / "With unstrung bow, pināka in hand, clad in a skin-garment."
They revere [it] until their breath is exhausted.

5.17.153.s: athāpo vyatiṣicya parāsya pātram anavekṣamāṇā āyanti
5.17.153.d: अथापो व्यतिषिच्य परास्य पात्रम् अनवेक्षमाणा आयन्ति
5.17.153.m: Then, having poured out water, and having thrown away the vessel, they return without looking back.

5.17.153.s: hastapādān prakṣālyaitenaiva yathetam ety ādityaṃ caruṃ punaretya nirvapati |
5.17.153.d: हस्तपादान् प्रक्षाल्यैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्य् आदित्यं चरुं पुनरेत्य निर्वपति ।
5.17.153.m: Having washed their hands and feet, having returned by the exact way they had gone, he returns and offers the caru oblation for Aditi.

5.17.153.s: iyaṃ vā aditir asyām eva pratitiṣṭhanti | iti brāhmaṇam | sā prasiddheṣṭiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate |
5.17.153.d: इयं वा अदितिर् अस्याम् एव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति । इति ब्राह्मणम् । सा प्रसिद्धेष्टिः संतिष्ठते ।
5.17.153.m: "Aditi indeed is this [earth]; in her verily they find support," so says a brāhmaṇa passage. That well-known offering is concluded.

5.17.153.s: atra visṛjate vratam atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvā yajamānāyatana upaviśya treṇyā śalalyā lohitāyasasya ca kṣureṇa śīrṣan ni ca vartayate pari ca vapate ya imāṃ mahīṃ pṛthivīm ṛtubhiḥ paryavartayat | yo asyāḥ pṛthivyās tvaci nivartayaty oṣadhīḥ | agnir īśāna ojasā varuṇo dhītibhiḥ saha | indro marudbhiḥ sakhibhiḥ saha || agnis tigmena śociṣā tapa ākrāntam uṣṇihā | śiras tapasy āhitam | vaiśvānarasya tejasā | ṛtenāsya nivartaye satyena parivartaye | tapasāsyānuvartaye śivenāsyopavartaye śagmenāsyābhivartaye || śīrṣṇas tad ṛtam | tat satyam | tad vratam | tac chakeyam | tena śakeyam | tena ādhyāsam iti purastād evāgre 'tha dakṣiṇato 'tha paścād athottarato 'thopariṣṭāt
5.17.153.d: अत्र विसृजते व्रतम् अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वा यजमानायतन उपविश्य त्रेण्या शलल्या लोहितायसस्य च क्षुरेण शीर्षन् नि च वर्तयते परि च वपते य इमां महीं पृथिवीम् ऋतुभिः पर्यवर्तयत् । यो अस्याः पृथिव्यास् त्वचि निवर्तयत्य् ओषधीः । अग्निर् ईशान ओजसा वरुणो धीतिभिः सह । इन्द्रो मरुद्भिः सखिभिः सह ॥ अग्निस् तिग्मेन शोचिषा तप आक्रान्तम् उष्णिहा । शिरस् तपस्य् आहितम् । वैश्वानरस्य तेजसा । ऋतेनास्य निवर्तये सत्येन परिवर्तये । तपसास्यानुवर्तये शिवेनास्योपवर्तये शग्मेनास्याभिवर्तये ॥ शीर्ष्णस् तद् ऋतम् । तत् सत्यम् । तद् व्रतम् । तच् छकेयम् । तेन शकेयम् । तेन आध्यासम् इति पुरस्ताद् एवाग्रे ऽथ दक्षिणतो ऽथ पश्चाद् अथोत्तरतो ऽथोपरिष्टात्
5.17.153.m: Here he releases the vow. Then, having offered the full moon and Vaimṛdha offerings, having sat down in the sacrificer's seat, he cuts and shaves the hair of the head with a three-striped porcupine quill and a copper razor: "He who revolved this great earth / through the seasons, / who upon the skin of this earth / rolls back the plants; / Agni ruling with might, / Varuṇa together with thoughts, / Indra together with his friends the Maruts; / Agni with sharp brilliance, / ascetic heat entered by the uṣṇih, / the head placed in heat / by the splendor of Vaiśvānara; / by Ṛta I roll it back from him, / by Truth I shave it around, / by ascetic heat I shave it after, / auspiciously I shave it near, / happily I shave it towards." From the head: "That is Ṛta," "That is Truth," "That is the vow," "May I be capable of that," "Thereby may I be capable," "Thereby may I prosper"—first on the front, then on the south, then on the west, then on the north, then on the top.

5.17.153.s: saṃtiṣṭhante sākamedhahavīm̐ṣi | idāvatsarīṇām̐ svastim āśāste | ity āśāste ||
5.17.153.d: संतिष्ठन्ते साकमेधहवीँषि । इदावत्सरीणाँ स्वस्तिम् आशास्ते । इत्य् आशास्ते ॥
5.17.153.m: The Sākamedha oblations are concluded. "He prays for the welfare of the Idāvatsara year," so he prays.

5.18.153.s: athātaś caturṣu māseṣu śunāsīrīyahavirbhir yakṣyamāṇo bhavati
5.18.153.d: अथातश् चतुर्षु मासेषु शुनासीरीयहविर्भिर् यक्ष्यमाणो भवति
5.18.153.m: Now at four months from this he will be about to sacrifice with the Śunāsīrīya oblations.

5.18.154.s: sa upakalpayate treṇīm̐ śalalīṃ lohitāyasasya ca kṣuraṃ pañcatayāni puroḍāśakapālāni pañca carusthālīs tāvanti mekṣaṇāni pṛṣadājyāya dadhīti |
5.18.154.d: स उपकल्पयते त्रेणीँ शललीं लोहितायसस्य च क्षुरं पञ्चतयानि पुरोडाशकपालानि पञ्च चरुस्थालीस् तावन्ति मेक्षणानि पृषदाज्याय दधीति ।
5.18.154.m: He procures a three-striped porcupine quill, a copper razor, five sets of cake-potsherds, five caru pots, as many stirring-sticks, and curds for the clotted ghee oblation.

5.18.154.s: athāsyaitām̐ rātriṃ vāyave vatsā apākṛtā bhavanti
5.18.154.d: अथास्यैताँ रात्रिं वायवे वत्सा अपाकृता भवन्ति
5.18.154.m: Then, on this night, calves are driven away for Vāyu.

5.18.154.s: prātarvāyavyaṃ payo dohayati saṃnāyyasya vāvṛtā tūṣṇīṃ vā |
5.18.154.d: प्रातर्वायव्यं पयो दोहयति संनाय्यस्य वावृता तूष्णीं वा ।
5.18.154.m: In the morning he milks the milk for Vāyu, either according to the rite of the curd-and-milk oblation or silently.

5.18.154.s: atha prātar hute 'gnihotre pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīya nirvapaty āgneyam aṣṭākapālam iti pañca saṃcarāṇy aindrāgnaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ carum indrāya śunāsīrāya puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vāyavyaṃ payaḥ sauryam ekakapālam iti
5.18.154.d: अथ प्रातर् हुते ऽग्निहोत्रे पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीय निर्वपत्य् आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालम् इति पञ्च संचराण्य् ऐन्द्राग्नं द्वादशकपालं वैश्वदेवं चरुम् इन्द्राय शुनासीराय पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं वायव्यं पयः सौर्यम् एककपालम् इति
5.18.154.m: Then, the agnihotra having been offered in the morning, having strewn the axial line and brought forward the waters, he measures out the five revolving offerings beginning with the eight-potsherd cake for Agni, a twelve-potsherd cake for Indra-Agni, a caru oblation for the All-gods, a twelve-potsherd cake for Indra Śunāsīra, the milk for Vāyu, and a one-potsherd cake for Sūrya.

5.18.154.s: tvacaṃ puroḍāśānāṃ grāhayitvā śrapayitvābhivāsya prāṅ etyāpyebhyo ninīya stambayajur harati |
5.18.154.d: त्वचं पुरोडाशानां ग्राहयित्वा श्रपयित्वाभिवास्य प्राङ् एत्याप्येभ्यो निनीय स्तम्बयजुर् हरति ।
5.18.154.m: Having caused the crust of the cakes to form, baked them, and covered them with hot ashes, having gone forward and poured out [water] for the Āpyas, he carries the stambayajus.
Just this is the well-known procedure relating to cake offerings.

5.18.154.s: trir yajuṣā tūṣṇīṃ caturtham | pūrvaṃ parigrāhaṃ parigṛhṇāti
5.18.154.d: त्रिर् यजुषा तूष्णीं चतुर्थम् । पूर्वं परिग्राहं परिगृह्णाति
5.18.154.m: Three times with a formula, silently the fourth time, he marks out the first boundary.

5.18.154.s: karaṇaṃ japati | uddhanti | uddhatād āgnīdhras trir harati sa yady uttaravediṃ karoti yathā mahāhavīm̐ṣy evam̐ saṃtiṣṭhate
5.18.154.d: करणं जपति । उद्धन्ति । उद्धताद् आग्नीध्रस् त्रिर् हरति स यद्य् उत्तरवेदिं करोति यथा महाहवीँष्य् एवँ संतिष्ठते
5.18.154.m: He murmurs the ritual tool [formula]. He digs up [the ground]. From the dug-up earth the āgnīdhra carries away [earth] three times. If he constructs an uttaravedi, it concludes in the manner of the Mahāhavis offerings.

5.18.154.s: yady u vā uttaravediṃ na karoti yathā vaiśvadevahavīm̐ṣy evam̐ saṃtiṣṭhte 'nyatra vājināt |
5.18.154.d: यद्य् उ वा उत्तरवेदिं न करोति यथा वैश्वदेवहवीँष्य् एवँ संतिष्ठ्ते ऽन्यत्र वाजिनात् ।
5.18.154.m: If, on the other hand, he does not construct an uttaravedi, it concludes in the manner of the Vaiśvadeva offerings, except for the vājina.
Then, having performed the full-vessel libation and the strides of Viṣṇu, he releases the vow.

5.18.154.s: atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvā yajamānāyatana upaviśya treṇyā śalalyā lohitāyasasya ca kṣureṇa śīrṣan ni ca vartayate pari ca vapate | ekaṃ māsam udasṛjat parameṣṭhī prajābhyaḥ | tenābhyo maha āvahat | amṛtaṃ martyābhyaḥ || prajām anu prajāyase tad u te martyāmṛtam | yena māsā ardhamāsās | ṛtavaḥ parivatsarāḥ || yena te te prajāpate ījānasya nyavartayan | tenāham asya brahmaṇā nivartayāmi jīvase || agnis tigmena śociṣā tapa ākrāntam uṣṇihā
5.18.154.d: अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वा यजमानायतन उपविश्य त्रेण्या शलल्या लोहितायसस्य च क्षुरेण शीर्षन् नि च वर्तयते परि च वपते । एकं मासम् उदसृजत् परमेष्ठी प्रजाभ्यः । तेनाभ्यो मह आवहत् । अमृतं मर्त्याभ्यः ॥ प्रजाम् अनु प्रजायसे तद् उ ते मर्त्यामृतम् । येन मासा अर्धमासास् । ऋतवः परिवत्सराः ॥ येन ते ते प्रजापते ईजानस्य न्यवर्तयन् । तेनाहम् अस्य ब्रह्मणा निवर्तयामि जीवसे ॥ अग्निस् तिग्मेन शोचिषा तप आक्रान्तम् उष्णिहा
5.18.154.m: Then, having sacrificed with the full-moon and Vaimṛdha offerings and sat in the sacrificer's place, he shaves downward and trims around the head with a three-striped porcupine quill and a copper razor: 'Parameṣṭhin released one month for the creatures; / thereby he brought great immortality to mortals. // You are born along with your offspring; / that indeed is your immortality, O mortal! // Whereby the months, the half-months, / the seasons, and the years [flow], // whereby, O Prajāpati, they shaved you / as you sacrificed, // by that sacred word of his / I shave [this one] that he may live. // Agni with sharp flame, / heat is approached by the Uṣṇih;'

5.18.155.s: śiras tapasy āhitam | vaiśvānarasya tejasā | ṛtenāsya nivartaye satyena parivartaye
5.18.155.d: शिरस् तपस्य् आहितम् । वैश्वानरस्य तेजसा । ऋतेनास्य निवर्तये सत्येन परिवर्तये
5.18.155.m: 'the head is placed in heat / by the splendor of Vaiśvānara; / through cosmic order I shave him downward, / through truth I shave around him,'

5.18.155.s: tapasāsyānuvartaye śivenāsyopavartaye śagmenāsyābhivartaye || śīṣṇas tad ṛtam | tat satyam | tad vratam | tac chakeyam | tena śakeyam | tena rādhyāsam iti purastād evāgre 'tha dakṣiṇato 'tha paścād athottarato 'thopariṣṭāt
5.18.155.d: तपसास्यानुवर्तये शिवेनास्योपवर्तये शग्मेनास्याभिवर्तये ॥ शीष्णस् तद् ऋतम् । तत् सत्यम् । तद् व्रतम् । तच् छकेयम् । तेन शकेयम् । तेन राध्यासम् इति पुरस्ताद् एवाग्रे ऽथ दक्षिणतो ऽथ पश्चाद् अथोत्तरतो ऽथोपरिष्टात्
5.18.155.m: 'through heat I shave after him, / auspiciously I shave toward him, / benevolently I shave upon him.' [He touches the hair] of the head: 'That is cosmic order, that is truth, that is the vow; may I be capable of that; with that may I be able; through that may I succeed'—first in front, then on the right, then behind, then on the north, then on top.
He hopes: 'He prays for well-being throughout the year.'

6.1.156.s: agniṣṭomena yakṣyamāṇo bhavati sa upakalpayate kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ ca vāsaś ca mekhalāṃ ca saiṣā pṛthvī veṇīkāryā bhavati trivṛdekataḥpāśā dvāvim̐śatiṃ ca darbhapuñjīlāni navanītaṃ cāñjanaṃ ca satūlāṃ ca śareṣīkām audumbaraṃ ca daṇḍaṃ camasaṃ ca vratapradānam̐ sthālīm̐ saśikyām̐ samekṣaṇām
6.1.156.d: अग्निष्टोमेन यक्ष्यमाणो भवति स उपकल्पयते कृष्णाजिनं च कृष्णविषाणां च वासश् च मेखलां च सैषा पृथ्वी वेणीकार्या भवति त्रिवृदेकतःपाशा द्वाविँशतिं च दर्भपुञ्जीलानि नवनीतं चाञ्जनं च सतूलां च शरेषीकाम् औदुम्बरं च दण्डं चमसं च व्रतप्रदानँ स्थालीँ सशिक्याँ समेक्षणाम्
6.1.156.m: When he is about to sacrifice with the Agniṣṭoma, he procures a black-antelope skin, a black-antelope horn, a garment, and a girdle—this is to be made wide, plaited, threefold, with a noose at one end—twenty-two darbha grass bunches, fresh butter, collyrium, a reed-stalk with tuft, an udumbara staff, a drinking-cup for giving the vow-drink, and a pot with a sling and a stirring stick.
These thirteen are for the sacrificer.

6.1.156.s: tāvanty eva patnīm abhito bhavanti kumbaṃ ca kurīraṃ ca vāsaś ca yoktraṃ cāparimitāni ca darbhapuñjīlāni navanītaṃ cāñjanaṃ ca satūlā ca śareṣīkāmṛnmayaś ca pātraḥ śaṅkuś ca sthālī saśikyā samekṣaṇā
6.1.156.d: तावन्त्य् एव पत्नीम् अभितो भवन्ति कुम्बं च कुरीरं च वासश् च योक्त्रं चापरिमितानि च दर्भपुञ्जीलानि नवनीतं चाञ्जनं च सतूला च शरेषीकामृन्मयश् च पात्रः शङ्कुश् च स्थाली सशिक्या समेक्षणा
6.1.156.m: There are just as many for the wife: a kumba head-ornament, a kurīra head-ornament, a garment, a yoke-halter, an unmeasured number of darbha grass bunches, fresh butter, collyrium, a reed-stalk with tuft, an earthen cup, a wooden peg, and a pot with a sling and a stirring stick.
A hall is erected on an approved sacrificial site.

6.1.156.s: purohaviṣi devayajane yājyed ity eteṣāṃ yaj joṣayate prācīnavam̐śā dikṣvatīkāśā dakṣiṇato varṣīyasī
6.1.156.d: पुरोहविषि देवयजने याज्येद् इत्य् एतेषां यज् जोषयते प्राचीनवँशा दिक्ष्वतीकाशा दक्षिणतो वर्षीयसी
6.1.156.m: 'One should sacrifice on a sacrificial site with the oblations to the east'—whichever of these he approves; its beams facing east, open to the quarters, wider to the south.

6.1.156.s: tasyai catasro dvāraḥ kurvanti prācīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ pratīcīm udīcīm |
6.1.156.d: तस्यै चतस्रो द्वारः कुर्वन्ति प्राचीं दक्षिणां प्रतीचीम् उदीचीम् ।
6.1.156.m: They make four doors for it: eastern, southern, western, and northern.
To the south they make a shed for boiling the vow-food; to the west, the wife's hall.

6.1.156.s: atha yadi dūre tīrthaṃ bhavaty uttareṇa śālāṃ dvau kaṭaparivārau kurvanti pūrvaṃ yajamānāyāparaṃ patnyai
6.1.156.d: अथ यदि दूरे तीर्थं भवत्य् उत्तरेण शालां द्वौ कटपरिवारौ कुर्वन्ति पूर्वं यजमानायापरं पत्न्यै
6.1.156.m: Now, if the water-place is far away, they construct two mat-enclosures north of the hall: the eastern one for the sacrificer, the western one for his wife.

6.1.156.s: tayoḥ prācī dvārau kurvanti tad udakumbhau nidhāpayati | athāmāvāsyena vā haviṣeṣṭvā nakṣatre vāraṇyor agnīn samārohya śālām abhipraiti |
6.1.156.d: तयोः प्राची द्वारौ कुर्वन्ति तद् उदकुम्भौ निधापयति । अथामावास्येन वा हविषेष्ट्वा नक्षत्रे वारण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य शालाम् अभिप्रैति ।
6.1.156.m: They make their doors facing east. There he has two water-jars placed. Then, having sacrificed with the new-moon oblation or under an auspicious constellation, having caused the fires to mount the two churning sticks, he proceeds toward the hall.

6.1.156.s: uttareṇa śālāṃ parītya pūrvayā dvārā śālāṃ prapādya gārhapatyasyāyatane mathitvāgnīn vihṛtya madhyame vam̐śe rājānaṃ pragrathnanti
6.1.156.d: उत्तरेण शालां परीत्य पूर्वया द्वारा शालां प्रपाद्य गार्हपत्यस्यायतने मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्य मध्यमे वँशे राजानं प्रग्रथ्नन्ति
6.1.156.m: Walking around north of the hall and entering the hall by the eastern door, having churned out [the fire] at the place of the gārhapatya and distributed the sacred fires, they tie King [Soma] to the central beam.

6.1.156.s: paristṛṇanti dakṣiṇata upaviśato brahmā ca yajamānaś ca | atha gārhapatya ājyaṃ vilāpyotpūya sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā saptahotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye juhoty anvārabdhe yajamāne svāhā | iti |
6.1.156.d: परिस्तृणन्ति दक्षिणत उपविशतो ब्रह्मा च यजमानश् च । अथ गार्हपत्य आज्यं विलाप्योत्पूय स्रुचि चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा सप्तहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये जुहोत्य् अन्वारब्धे यजमाने स्वाहा । इति ।
6.1.156.m: They strew [grass] around. To the south sit both the Brahman and the sacrificer. Then, having melted the clarified butter on the gārhapatya and purified it, having taken four portions in the ladle and recited mentally the Saptahotṛ formula, he offers on the āhavanīya while the sacrificer holds onto him: 'Svāhā!'

6.1.157.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā yūpāhutiṃ juhoti yady atra juhoti
6.1.157.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा यूपाहुतिं जुहोति यद्य् अत्र जुहोति
6.1.157.m: Having taken another four portions, he offers the sacrificial post libation, if he offers it here.

6.1.157.s: pūrvāhṇa evaitau vratadughayor vatsau badhnanti | athābhyāṃ vratopāyanīyaṃ pācayati
6.1.157.d: पूर्वाह्ण एवैतौ व्रतदुघयोर् वत्सौ बध्नन्ति । अथाभ्यां व्रतोपायनीयं पाचयति
6.1.157.m: In the forenoon itself they tie the two calves of the vow-milking cows. Then he has the food for entering the vow cooked for the two.

6.1.157.s: tasyāśitau bhavataḥ sarpirmiśrasya payomiśrasya | athādhvaryus tīrthyān saṃbhārān yācati |
6.1.157.d: तस्याशितौ भवतः सर्पिर्मिश्रस्य पयोमिश्रस्य । अथाध्वर्युस् तीर्थ्यान् संभारान् याचति ।
6.1.157.m: They eat of it, mixed with ghee and mixed with milk. Then the adhvaryu priest asks for the requisites from the water-place.

6.1.157.s: athāha | ehi yajamāna | iti pūrvayā dvāropaniṣkramya yatrāpas tad yanti |
6.1.157.d: अथाह । एहि यजमान । इति पूर्वया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य यत्रापस् तद् यन्ति ।
6.1.157.m: Then he says, 'Come, sacrificer!' Having gone out by the eastern door, they go to where water is.

6.1.157.s: athāsya prāṅmukhasya dakṣiṇaṃ godānam adbhir unatti ||
6.1.157.d: अथास्य प्राङ्मुखस्य दक्षिणं गोदानम् अद्भिर् उनत्ति ॥
6.1.157.m: Then, as he faces east, he moistens his right side of the head with water:

6.2.157.s: āpa undantu jīvase dīrghāyutvāya varcase | iti | ūrdhvāgraṃ barhir anūcchrayati | oṣadhe trāyasvainam iti
6.2.157.d: आप उन्दन्तु जीवसे दीर्घायुत्वाय वर्चसे । इति । ऊर्ध्वाग्रं बर्हिर् अनूच्छ्रयति । ओषधे त्रायस्वैनम् इति
6.2.157.m: 'May the waters moisten you for life, for longevity, for luster.' He places along it a blade of sacrificial grass pointing upward: 'O plant, protect him!'

6.2.157.s: svadhitiṃ tiryañcaṃ nidadhāti svadhite mainam̐ him̐sīs | iti
6.2.157.d: स्वधितिं तिर्यञ्चं निदधाति स्वधिते मैनँ हिँसीस् । इति
6.2.157.m: He lays the razor crosswise: 'O razor, harm him not!'
He shaves: 'Pleasing to the gods, I shave these.'

6.2.157.s: svasty uttarāṇy aśīya | ity uptāntaṃ pratyabhimṛśate | etayaivāvṛtottaraṃ godānam adbhir unatti yajuṣā vā tūṣṇīṃ vā
6.2.157.d: स्वस्त्य् उत्तराण्य् अशीय । इत्य् उप्तान्तं प्रत्यभिमृशते । एतयैवावृतोत्तरं गोदानम् अद्भिर् उनत्ति यजुषा वा तूष्णीं वा
6.2.157.m: 'May I attain further welfare,' saying this, he touches the end of the shaved part. In this very manner he moistens the northern side of the head with water, either with a formula or silently.

6.2.157.s: nāpitāya kṣuraṃ prayacchann āha nāpitoptakeśaśmaśruṃ me nikṛttanakhaṃ prabrūtāt | iti
6.2.157.d: नापिताय क्षुरं प्रयच्छन्न् आह नापितोप्तकेशश्मश्रुं मे निकृत्तनखं प्रब्रूतात् । इति
6.2.157.m: Handing over the razor to the barber, he says, 'Barber, announce me when the hair and beard have been shaved and the nails paired!'

6.2.157.s: athainam adbhir abhiṣiñcati | āpo asmān mātaraḥ śundhantu ghṛtena no ghṛtapuvaḥ punantu | iti
6.2.157.d: अथैनम् अद्भिर् अभिषिञ्चति । आपो अस्मान् मातरः शुन्धन्तु घृतेन नो घृतपुवः पुनन्तु । इति
6.2.157.m: Then he pours water over him: 'May the waters, our mothers, cleanse us; may they who purify with ghee purify us with ghee.'

6.2.157.s: saṃpradhāvya rajaḥ praplāvayati viśvam asmat pravahantu ripram iti |
6.2.157.d: संप्रधाव्य रजः प्रप्लावयति विश्वम् अस्मत् प्रवहन्तु रिप्रम् इति ।
6.2.157.m: Washing thoroughly, he washes away the dirt: 'May they carry away all impurity from us.'

6.2.157.s: udeti | ud ābhyaḥ śucir ā pūta emi | iti vasanasyāntena praticchādyāpa ācāmati |
6.2.157.d: उदेति । उद् आभ्यः शुचिर् आ पूत एमि । इति वसनस्यान्तेन प्रतिच्छाद्याप आचामति ।
6.2.157.m: He steps out: 'Pure and cleansed, I step up out of these.' Covering himself with the edge of the garment, he sips water.

6.2.157.s: apo 'śnāt | iti brāhmaṇam atha pradakṣiṇam ahataṃ vāsaḥ paridhatte somasya tanūr asi tanuvaṃ me pāhi | iti |
6.2.157.d: अपो ऽश्नात् । इति ब्राह्मणम् अथ प्रदक्षिणम् अहतं वासः परिधत्ते सोमस्य तनूर् असि तनुवं मे पाहि । इति ।
6.2.157.m: 'He sips water,' thus says the brāhmaṇa passage. Then, clockwise, he puts on an unwashed garment: 'You are the body of Soma; protect my body.'
Then this fresh butter of his, gathered together, rests in a water-saucer.

6.2.157.s: tasya pāṇibhyām̐ saṃpramlāya mukham eva prathamam abhyaṅkte mahīnāṃ payo 'si varcodhā asi varco mayi dhehi | iti |
6.2.157.d: तस्य पाणिभ्याँ संप्रम्लाय मुखम् एव प्रथमम् अभ्यङ्क्ते महीनां पयो ऽसि वर्चोधा असि वर्चो मयि धेहि । इति ।
6.2.157.m: Rubbing it with both hands, he anoints his face first: 'You are the milk of the great ones; you are the bestower of luster; bestow luster in me.'

6.2.158.s: anulomam ā pādābhyām anyo 'sya pṛṣṭham abhyanakti | athāsyaitad āñjanaṃ piṣṭaṃ dṛṣady upaśete satūlā ca śareṣīkā
6.2.158.d: अनुलोमम् आ पादाभ्याम् अन्यो ऽस्य पृष्ठम् अभ्यनक्ति । अथास्यैतद् आञ्जनं पिष्टं दृषद्य् उपशेते सतूला च शरेषीका
6.2.158.m: Following the grain down to the feet. Another person anoints his back. Then this collyrium of his, ground, rests on the mill-stone, along with the tufted reed-stalk.

6.2.158.s: tasya prāṅmukhasya pratyaṅmukha upaviśya savyena pāṇinā dakṣiṇam akṣy anakti vṛtrasya kanīnikāsi cakṣuṣpā asi cakṣur me pāhi | iti trir anidhāvam |
6.2.158.d: तस्य प्राङ्मुखस्य प्रत्यङ्मुख उपविश्य सव्येन पाणिना दक्षिणम् अक्ष्य् अनक्ति वृत्रस्य कनीनिकासि चक्षुष्पा असि चक्षुर् मे पाहि । इति त्रिर् अनिधावम् ।
6.2.158.m: Sitting down facing west in front of him who faces east, with the left hand he anoints his right eye: 'You are the pupil of Vṛtra; you are the protector of the eye; protect my eye'—three times, without running over.

6.2.158.s: dvir uttaram apy u pañca kṛtva āṅkte | iti brāhmaṇam | pañca kṛtva eva dakṣiṇaṃ pañca kṛtva uttaram
6.2.158.d: द्विर् उत्तरम् अप्य् उ पञ्च कृत्व आङ्क्ते । इति ब्राह्मणम् । पञ्च कृत्व एव दक्षिणं पञ्च कृत्व उत्तरम्
6.2.158.m: Twice the left eye. There is also the brāhmaṇa passage: 'He anoints five times.' Exactly five times the right, five times the left.

6.2.158.s: athainam ekavim̐śatyā darbhapuñjīlaiḥ pavayati citpatis tvā punātu vākpatis tvā punātu devas tvā savitā punātv acchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhis | iti
6.2.158.d: अथैनम् एकविँशत्या दर्भपुञ्जीलैः पवयति चित्पतिस् त्वा पुनातु वाक्पतिस् त्वा पुनातु देवस् त्वा सविता पुनात्व् अच्छिद्रेण पवित्रेण वसोः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिस् । इति
6.2.158.m: Then he purifies him with twenty-one darbha grass bunches: 'May the lord of thought purify you; may the lord of speech purify you; may divine Savitar purify you, with an unbroken purifier, with the rays of the good sun.'

6.2.158.s: yajamānam ativācayati tasya te pavitrapate pavitreṇa yasmai kaṃ pune tac chakeyam iti |
6.2.158.d: यजमानम् अतिवाचयति तस्य ते पवित्रपते पवित्रेण यस्मै कं पुने तच् छकेयम् इति ।
6.2.158.m: He makes the sacrificer recite: 'With the purifier of you, the lord of the purifier, for whatever purpose I purify myself, may I be able to accomplish that.'

6.2.158.s: athainam̐ savye pāṇāv abhipātya śālām ānayati | ā vo devāsa īmahe satyadharmāṇo adhvare yad vo devāsa āgure yajñiyāso havāmahe | iti
6.2.158.d: अथैनँ सव्ये पाणाव् अभिपात्य शालाम् आनयति । आ वो देवास ईमहे सत्यधर्माणो अध्वरे यद् वो देवास आगुरे यज्ञियासो हवामहे । इति
6.2.158.m: Then, taking him by the left hand, he leads him to the sacrificial hall with: 'To you, O gods whose laws are true, we come at the sacrifice; since, O worshipful gods, we call upon your consent.'

6.2.158.s: pūrvayā dvārā śālāṃ prapādayati | indrāgnī dyāvāpṛthivī āpa oṣadhīs | iti |
6.2.158.d: पूर्वया द्वारा शालां प्रपादयति । इन्द्राग्नी द्यावापृथिवी आप ओषधीस् । इति ।
6.2.158.m: He makes him enter the sacrificial hall through the eastern door with: 'Indra and Agni, heaven and earth, waters, plants.'

6.2.158.s: athainam agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāṇīya dakṣiṇata udaṅmukham upaveśyāhavanīyam īkṣayati tvaṃ dīkṣāṇām adhipatir asi | iti |
6.2.158.d: अथैनम् अग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याणीय दक्षिणत उदङ्मुखम् उपवेश्याहवनीयम् ईक्षयति त्वं दीक्षाणाम् अधिपतिर् असि । इति ।
6.2.158.m: Then, having led him around in front of the āhavanīya fire and made him sit down to the south facing north, he makes him look at the āhavanīya fire with: 'You are the overlord of consecrations.'

6.2.158.s: iha mā santaṃ pāhi | ity ātmānam ||
6.2.158.d: इह मा सन्तं पाहि । इत्य् आत्मानम् ॥
6.2.158.m: With: 'Protect me while I am here,' [the sacrificer looks at] himself.

6.3.158.s: yāvadevātrādhvaryuś ceṣṭati tāvad eṣa pratiprasthātā patnyai dakṣiṇam upapakṣam adbhir unatti tūṣṇīm |
6.3.158.d: यावदेवात्राध्वर्युश् चेष्टति तावद् एष प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्न्यै दक्षिणम् उपपक्षम् अद्भिर् उनत्ति तूष्णीम् ।
6.3.158.m: While the adhvaryu priest is busy here, the pratiprasthātṛ priest silently moistens the right armpit of the [sacrificer's] wife with water.
Silently he holds sacrificial grass pointing upwards beside it.

6.3.158.s: tūṣṇīm̐ svadhitiṃ tiryañcaṃ nidadhāti tūṣṇīṃ pravapati tūṣṇīm uptāntaṃ pratyabhimṛśate |
6.3.158.d: तूष्णीँ स्वधितिं तिर्यञ्चं निदधाति तूष्णीं प्रवपति तूष्णीम् उप्तान्तं प्रत्यभिमृशते ।
6.3.158.m: Silently he applies the razor crosswise; silently he shaves; silently he touches the edge of what has been shaved.

6.3.158.s: etayaivāvṛtottaram upapakṣam adbhir unatti tūṣṇīm eva
6.3.158.d: एतयैवावृतोत्तरम् उपपक्षम् अद्भिर् उनत्ति तूष्णीम् एव
6.3.158.m: In this very same manner, he silently moistens the left armpit with water.

6.3.158.s: nāpitāya kṣuraṃ prayacchann āha nāpitoptopapakṣāṃ me nikṛttanakhāṃ prabrūtāt | iti
6.3.158.d: नापिताय क्षुरं प्रयच्छन्न् आह नापितोप्तोपपक्षां मे निकृत्तनखां प्रब्रूतात् । इति
6.3.158.m: Handing the razor to the barber, he says: 'O barber, announce to me when her armpits are shaved and her nails are pared.'

6.3.158.s: tāṃ tathā prāha | athainām adbhir abhiṣiñcati tūṣṇīm |
6.3.158.d: तां तथा प्राह । अथैनाम् अद्भिर् अभिषिञ्चति तूष्णीम् ।
6.3.158.m: He announces to him that she is so [prepared]. Then he silently pours water over her.

6.3.159.s: tūṣṇīm̐ saṃpradhāvya rajaḥ praplāvayati tūṣṇīm adbhir udeti tūṣṇīm |
6.3.159.d: तूष्णीँ संप्रधाव्य रजः प्रप्लावयति तूष्णीम् अद्भिर् उदेति तूष्णीम् ।
6.3.159.m: Silently washing herself, she washes away the dirt; silently she steps out of the water.

6.3.159.s: vasanasyāntena praticchādyāpa ācāmati tūṣṇīṃ pradakṣiṇam ahataṃ vāsaḥ paridhatte
6.3.159.d: वसनस्यान्तेन प्रतिच्छाद्याप आचामति तूष्णीं प्रदक्षिणम् अहतं वासः परिधत्ते
6.3.159.m: Covering herself with the hem of her garment, she sips water; silently, moving from left to right, she puts on an unwashed garment.
Silently she anoints [her body]; silently she collies [her eyes].

6.3.159.s: athainām aparimitair darbhapuñjīlaiḥ pavayati tūṣṇīṃtūṣṇīm eva | athainām ānīyāparayā dvārā śālāṃ prapādya prācīm udānayan vācayati praitu brahmaṇaspatnī vediṃ varṇena sīdatu | athāham anukāminī sve loke viśā iha | iti |
6.3.159.d: अथैनाम् अपरिमितैर् दर्भपुञ्जीलैः पवयति तूष्णींतूष्णीम् एव । अथैनाम् आनीयापरया द्वारा शालां प्रपाद्य प्राचीम् उदानयन् वाचयति प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पत्नी वेदिं वर्णेन सीदतु । अथाहम् अनुकामिनी स्वे लोके विशा इह । इति ।
6.3.159.m: Then he purifies her with an unmeasured number of darbha bunches, each time silently. Then, having led her and made her enter the sacrificial hall through the western door, leading her forward towards the east, he makes her recite: 'May the wife of the Brahmin go forward; let her sit upon the altar with beauty. Then may I, following my desire, enter here into my own world.'

6.3.159.s: atha jaghanena gārhapatyam upasīdati suprajasas tvā vayam | supatnīr upasedima | agne sapatnadambhanam adabdhāso adābhyam iti |
6.3.159.d: अथ जघनेन गार्हपत्यम् उपसीदति सुप्रजसस् त्वा वयम् । सुपत्नीर् उपसेदिम । अग्ने सपत्नदम्भनम् अदब्धासो अदाभ्यम् इति ।
6.3.159.m: Then she sits down behind the gārhapatya fire with: 'With good offspring may we, with good wives, sit beside you, O Agni, who confound rivals, unfoiled [beside you] who cannot be foiled.'

6.3.159.s: atha pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyāgnāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ dīkṣaṇīyām iṣṭiṃ nirvapati
6.3.159.d: अथ पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयाग्नावैष्णवम् एकादशकपालं दीक्षणीयाम् इष्टिं निर्वपति
6.3.159.m: Then, having strewn [sacrificial grass] along the spine-line and carried forward the waters, he measures out the oblation for the consecration ritual, [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu.

6.3.159.s: tasyai daśatayam utsīdati na yajamānaṃ vratam upanayati na patnīm̐ saṃnahyati na yajamānabhāgaṃ karoti na brahmabhāgaṃ na barhiṣadaṃ puroḍāśaṃ karoti nānvāhāryaṃ yācati na phalīkaraṇahomena carati na samiṣṭayajur juhoti na pūrṇapātre yajamānaṃ vācayati na viṣṇukramān kramate |
6.3.159.d: तस्यै दशतयम् उत्सीदति न यजमानं व्रतम् उपनयति न पत्नीँ संनह्यति न यजमानभागं करोति न ब्रह्मभागं न बर्हिषदं पुरोडाशं करोति नान्वाहार्यं याचति न फलीकरणहोमेन चरति न समिष्टयजुर् जुहोति न पूर्णपात्रे यजमानं वाचयति न विष्णुक्रमान् क्रमते ।
6.3.159.m: A decade [of rites] is omitted from it: he does not induct the sacrificer into the vow; he does not gird the wife; he does not assign the sacrificer's share; he does not assign the Brahman's share; he does not place the cake upon the sacrificial grass; he does not ask for the anvāhārya cooked rice; he does not perform the offering of the husks; he does not offer the samiṣṭayajus libation; he does not make the sacrificer recite over the full vessel; he does not take the Viṣṇu-strides.

6.3.159.s: athādhvayuḥ pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya pratyaṅṅ ādrutya patnīḥ saṃyājya prāṅ etya dhruvām āpyāyyājyasthālyāṃ pratyavanīyājyasthālyāḥ sruveṇopaghātaṃ dīkṣāhutīr juhoti ||
6.3.159.d: अथाध्वयुः प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य प्रत्यङ्ङ् आद्रुत्य पत्नीः संयाज्य प्राङ् एत्य ध्रुवाम् आप्याय्याज्यस्थाल्यां प्रत्यवनीयाज्यस्थाल्याः स्रुवेणोपघातं दीक्षाहुतीर् जुहोति ॥
6.3.159.m: Then the adhvaryu priest, having turned from left to right, running westward, having performed the offerings to the wives of the gods, going eastward, having replenished the dhruvā ladle, having poured [melted butter] back into the butter-pot, offers the consecration libations with the sruva dipping-spoon scooping from the butter-pot:

6.4.159.s: ākūtyai prayuje 'gnaye svāhā medhāyai manase 'gnaye svāhā dīkṣāyai tapase 'gnaye svāhā sarasvatyai pūṣṇe 'gnaye svāhā | iti |
6.4.159.d: आकूत्यै प्रयुजे ऽग्नये स्वाहा मेधायै मनसे ऽग्नये स्वाहा दीक्षायै तपसे ऽग्नये स्वाहा सरस्वत्यै पूष्णे ऽग्नये स्वाहा । इति ।
6.4.159.m: 'To intention, the yoke-fellow, to Agni, svāhā! To wisdom, to thought, to Agni, svāhā! To consecration, to austerity, to Agni, svāhā! To Sarasvatī, to Pūṣan, to Agni, svāhā!'

6.4.159.s: atha sruci caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā srucā pañcamīṃ juhoti | āpo devīr bṛhatīr viśvaśambhuvo dyāvāpṛthivī urv antarikṣaṃ bṛhaspatir no haviṣā vṛdhātu svāhā | iti |
6.4.159.d: अथ स्रुचि चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा स्रुचा पञ्चमीं जुहोति । आपो देवीर् बृहतीर् विश्वशम्भुवो द्यावापृथिवी उर्व् अन्तरिक्षं बृहस्पतिर् नो हविषा वृधातु स्वाहा । इति ।
6.4.159.m: Then, having taken four ladlings in the sruc ladle, he offers the fifth [libation] with the sruc ladle: 'May the divine waters, lofty, beneficial to all, heaven and earth, and the broad intermediate space, may Bṛhaspati increase us with the oblation, svāhā!'

6.4.160.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvājyasya pūrṇām̐ srucam audgrahaṇaṃ juhoti visve devasya netur marto vṛṇīta sakhyam | viśve rāya iṣudhyasi dyumnaṃ vṛṇīta puṣyase svāhā | iti |
6.4.160.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वाज्यस्य पूर्णाँ स्रुचम् औद्ग्रहणं जुहोति विस्वे देवस्य नेतुर् मर्तो वृणीत सख्यम् । विश्वे राय इषुध्यसि द्युम्नं वृणीत पुष्यसे स्वाहा । इति ।
6.4.160.m: Having taken another four ladlings, he offers the elevating libation with the sruc ladle full of melted butter: 'May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader; every one demands wealth; may he choose glory that he may thrive, svāhā!'
At this point he pours out this full vessel inside the altar.

6.4.160.s: athāgreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya yajamānāya prayacchati kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ ca vāsaś ca mekhalāṃ caudumbaraṃ daṇḍaṃ pañcamam uṣṇīṣam̐ ṣaṣṭham
6.4.160.d: अथाग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य यजमानाय प्रयच्छति कृष्णाजिनं च कृष्णविषाणां च वासश् च मेखलां चौदुम्बरं दण्डं पञ्चमम् उष्णीषँ षष्ठम्
6.4.160.m: Then, having carried them around in front of the āhavanīya fire, he hands to the sacrificer the black antelope skin, the black antelope horn, the garment, the girdle, an udumbara staff as the fifth, and a turban as the sixth.

6.4.160.s: atha pratiprasthātā patnyai prayacchati kumbaṃ ca kurīraṃ ca vāsaś ca yoktraṃ ca śaṅkuṃ ca ||
6.4.160.d: अथ प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति कुम्बं च कुरीरं च वासश् च योक्त्रं च शङ्कुं च ॥
6.4.160.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ priest hands to the [sacrificer's] wife the head-net, the hair-net, the garment, the yoke-cord, and the wooden peg.

6.5.160.m: Then at the sacrificer's seat, he spreads out the black antelope skin with its neck pointing eastward and its hairy side turned upwards.

6.5.160.s: tasya śuklakṛṣṇe saṃmṛśati śukle 'ṅguṣṭho bhavati kṛṣṇe 'ṅgulir ṛksāmayoḥ śilpe sthas te vām ārabhe te mā pātam āsya yajñasyodṛcas | iti |
6.5.160.d: तस्य शुक्लकृष्णे संमृशति शुक्ले ऽङ्गुष्ठो भवति कृष्णे ऽङ्गुलिर् ऋक्सामयोः शिल्पे स्थस् ते वाम् आरभे ते मा पातम् आस्य यज्ञस्योदृचस् । इति ।
6.5.160.m: He touches its white and black [spots]—the thumb is on the white, the finger on the black—with: 'You two are the artful forms of Ṛgveda and Sāmaveda; I take hold of you two; protect me until the completion of this sacrifice.'

6.5.160.s: atha dakṣiṇaṃ jānvācyābhisarpati | imāṃ dhiyam̐ śikṣamāṇasya deva kratuṃ dakṣaṃ varuṇa sam̐śiśādhi | yayāti viśvā duritā tarema sutarmāṇam adhi nāvam̐ ruhema | iti |
6.5.160.d: अथ दक्षिणं जान्वाच्याभिसर्पति । इमां धियँ शिक्षमाणस्य देव क्रतुं दक्षं वरुण सँशिशाधि । ययाति विश्वा दुरिता तरेम सुतर्माणम् अधि नावँ रुहेम । इति ।
6.5.160.m: Then, having bent the right knee, he creeps towards it with: 'O god Varuṇa, sharpen this thought, the will and power of the one who strives; by which may we cross over all evils, may we mount the boat that carries well across.'

6.5.160.s: athopasthaṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ mekhalāṃ paryasyati | ūrgasy āṅgirasy ūrṇamradā ūrjaṃ me yaccha | iti
6.5.160.d: अथोपस्थं कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं मेखलां पर्यस्यति । ऊर्गस्य् आङ्गिरस्य् ऊर्णम्रदा ऊर्जं मे यच्छ । इति
6.5.160.m: Then, having made a lap, he winds the girdle around [himself] from left to right with: 'You are strength, Angiras-like, soft as wool; grant me strength.'

6.5.160.s: pāhi mā mā mā him̐sīs | iti niṣṭarkyaṃ granthiṃ grathnāti | etasmin kāle pratiprasthātā yoktreṇa patnīm̐ saṃnahyati | āśāsānā saumanasam | saṃ tvā nahyāmi | iti dvābhyām
6.5.160.d: पाहि मा मा मा हिँसीस् । इति निष्टर्क्यं ग्रन्थिं ग्रथ्नाति । एतस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता योक्त्रेण पत्नीँ संनह्यति । आशासाना सौमनसम् । सं त्वा नह्यामि । इति द्वाभ्याम्
6.5.160.m: With: 'Protect me, do not harm me,' he ties a slipknot. At this time the pratiprasthātṛ priest girds the wife with the yoke-cord with the two [formulas]: 'Hoping for good will...' and 'I gird you...'

6.5.160.s: atha yajamānaṃ vāsasā prorṇoti viṣṇoḥ śarmāsi śarma yajamānasya śarma me yaccha | iti
6.5.160.d: अथ यजमानं वाससा प्रोर्णोति विष्णोः शर्मासि शर्म यजमानस्य शर्म मे यच्छ । इति
6.5.160.m: Then he covers the sacrificer with the garment with: 'You are Viṣṇu's shelter, the sacrificer's shelter; grant me shelter.'

6.5.160.s: vasanasyātīkāśeṣu vācayati nakṣatrāṇāṃ mātīkāśāt pāhi | iti
6.5.160.d: वसनस्यातीकाशेषु वाचयति नक्षत्राणां मातीकाशात् पाहि । इति
6.5.160.m: He makes him recite over the seams of the garment: 'Protect me from the shining of the constellations.'

6.5.160.s: pratikṛṣya vasanasyāntān pradakṣiṇam uṣṇīṣeṇa śiro veṣṭayati śriyā te śiro veṣṭayāmi śriyai yaśase brahmavarcasāya | iti |
6.5.160.d: प्रतिकृष्य वसनस्यान्तान् प्रदक्षिणम् उष्णीषेण शिरो वेष्टयति श्रिया ते शिरो वेष्टयामि श्रियै यशसे ब्रह्मवर्चसाय । इति ।
6.5.160.m: Having drawn back the ends of the garment, he wraps the head from left to right with the turban with: 'With prosperity I wrap your head, for prosperity, for fame, for holy luster.'

6.5.161.s: etasmin kāle pratiprasthātā patnyai kumbakurīram adhyūhati tūṣṇīm
6.5.161.d: एतस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्न्यै कुम्बकुरीरम् अध्यूहति तूष्णीम्
6.5.161.m: At this time the pratiprasthātṛ priest silently puts the head-net and hair-net on the [sacrificer's] wife.

6.5.161.s: athāsyaiṣā kṛṣṇaviṣāṇā trivalir vā pañcavalir vā śāṇyā rajjvā paritṛṇā maṇḍacaravad vigrathitā
6.5.161.d: अथास्यैषा कृष्णविषाणा त्रिवलिर् वा पञ्चवलिर् वा शाण्या रज्ज्वा परितृणा मण्डचरवद् विग्रथिता
6.5.161.m: Then this black antelope horn of his has three folds or five folds, is pierced around with a hempen cord, and is knotted like a head ornament.

6.5.161.s: tāṃ yajamānāya prayacchati | indrasya yonir asi | iti
6.5.161.d: तां यजमानाय प्रयच्छति । इन्द्रस्य योनिर् असि । इति
6.5.161.m: He gives it to the sacrificer with: 'You are Indra's womb.'

6.5.161.s: mā mā him̐sīs | iti yajamānaḥ pratigṛhṇāti tāṃ vasanasyāntamāyāṃ daśāyāṃ baddhvā tayāntarvedi loṣṭam uddhanti kṛṣyai tvā susasyāyai | iti
6.5.161.d: मा मा हिँसीस् । इति यजमानः प्रतिगृह्णाति तां वसनस्यान्तमायां दशायां बद्ध्वा तयान्तर्वेदि लोष्टम् उद्धन्ति कृष्यै त्वा सुसस्यायै । इति
6.5.161.m: The sacrificer receives it with: 'Do not harm me.' Having tied it to the outermost fringe of the garment, he digs up a clod [of earth] inside the altar with it, with: 'For agriculture, for good crops [I dig] you.'

6.5.161.s: supippalābhyas tvauṣadhībhyas | iti dakṣiṇaṃ godānaṃ kaṇḍūyate |
6.5.161.d: सुपिप्पलाभ्यस् त्वौषधीभ्यस् । इति दक्षिणं गोदानं कण्डूयते ।
6.5.161.m: With: 'For plants with good fruit [I scratch] you,' he scratches the right side of his head.

6.5.161.s: etasmin kāle pratiprasthātā patnyai śaṅkum ābadhnāti | etena kaṇḍūyasva | iti |
6.5.161.d: एतस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्न्यै शङ्कुम् आबध्नाति । एतेन कण्डूयस्व । इति ।
6.5.161.m: At this time the pratiprasthātṛ priest ties the wooden peg to the [sacrificer's] wife, saying: 'Scratch yourself with this.'

6.5.161.s: athāsmā ūrdhvāgram audumbaraṃ daṇḍaṃ prayacchati mukhena saṃmitam | sūpasthā devo vanaspatis | iti |
6.5.161.d: अथास्मा ऊर्ध्वाग्रम् औदुम्बरं दण्डं प्रयच्छति मुखेन संमितम् । सूपस्था देवो वनस्पतिस् । इति ।
6.5.161.m: Then he hands him an udumbara staff pointing upwards, equal to his mouth in height, with: 'A good refuge is the divine tree.'

6.5.161.s: ūrdhvo mā pāhy odṛcas | iti yajamānaḥ pratigṛhṇāti |
6.5.161.d: ऊर्ध्वो मा पाह्य् ओदृचस् । इति यजमानः प्रतिगृह्णाति ।
6.5.161.m: The sacrificer receives it with: 'Standing upright, protect me until the completion [of the sacrifice].'

6.5.161.s: athainaṃ yajñasyānvārambhaṃ vācayati svāhā yajñaṃ manasā svāhā dyāvāpṛthivībhyām̐ svāhoror antarikṣāt svāhā yajñaṃ vātād ārabhe | iti |
6.5.161.d: अथैनं यज्ञस्यान्वारम्भं वाचयति स्वाहा यज्ञं मनसा स्वाहा द्यावापृथिवीभ्याँ स्वाहोरोर् अन्तरिक्षात् स्वाहा यज्ञं वाताद् आरभे । इति ।
6.5.161.m: Then he makes him recite the taking hold of the sacrifice: 'Svāhā! The sacrifice with the mind; svāhā! from heaven and earth; svāhā! from the broad intermediate space; svāhā! I take hold of the sacrifice from the wind.'
Here he clenches his fists and restrains his speech.

6.5.161.s: athāha | adīkṣiṣṭāyaṃ brāhmaṇo 'sāv itthaṃgotro 'muṣya putro 'muṣya pautro 'muṣya naptā tam indrāyendrāgnibhyāṃ vasubhyo rudrebhya ādityebhyo viśvebho devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaś ca somapebhyaḥ prabrūmas | iti
6.5.161.d: अथाह । अदीक्षिष्टायं ब्राह्मणो ऽसाव् इत्थंगोत्रो ऽमुष्य पुत्रो ऽमुष्य पौत्रो ऽमुष्य नप्ता तम् इन्द्रायेन्द्राग्निभ्यां वसुभ्यो रुद्रेभ्य आदित्येभ्यो विश्वेभो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यश् च सोमपेभ्यः प्रब्रूमस् । इति
6.5.161.m: Then he says: 'This brāhmaṇa, so-and-so, of such-and-such lineage, son of so-and-so, grandson of so-and-so, great-grandson of so-and-so, has been consecrated. We announce him to Indra, to Indrāgnī, to the Vasus, to the Rudras, to the Ādityas, to the All-gods, and to the soma-drinking brāhmaṇas.'

6.5.162.s: trir upām̐śv āha devebhya evainaṃ prāha trir uccair upaniṣkramya |
6.5.162.d: त्रिर् उपाँश्व् आह देवेभ्य एवैनं प्राह त्रिर् उच्चैर् उपनिष्क्रम्य ।
6.5.162.m: He says it three times silently; he announces him to the gods alone. Having stepped out, [he says it] three times aloud.

6.5.162.s: ubhayebhya evainaṃ devamanuṣyebhyaḥ prāha | iti brāhmaṇam athainam̐ sam̐śāsti ||
6.5.162.d: उभयेभ्य एवैनं देवमनुष्येभ्यः प्राह । इति ब्राह्मणम् अथैनँ सँशास्ति ॥
6.5.162.m: 'He announces him to both, indeed to gods and men,' says the brāhmaṇa passage. Then he instructs him:

6.6.162.s: dīkṣito 'si dīkṣitavādaṃ vada satyam eva vada mānṛtam | mā smayiṣṭhās | mā kaṇḍūyathās | māpāvṛthās | yadi smayāsā apigṛhya smayāsai yadi kaṇḍūyāsai kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā kaṇḍūyāsai yadi vācaṃ visṛjer vaiṣṇavīm ṛcam anudravatāt | mā tvānyatra dīkṣitavimitāt sūryo 'bhyudiyāt | mābhinimruktāt | yāni devatānāmāni yathākhyātaṃ tāny ācakṣvātha yāny adevatānāmāni yathākhyātaṃ tāny ācakṣāṇa upariṣṭād vicakṣaṇaṃ dhehi canasitavatīṃ vicakṣaṇavatīṃ vācaṃ vada kṛṣṇājinān mā vyavacchetthā daṇḍāc ca | iti
6.6.162.d: दीक्षितो ऽसि दीक्षितवादं वद सत्यम् एव वद मानृतम् । मा स्मयिष्ठास् । मा कण्डूयथास् । मापावृथास् । यदि स्मयासा अपिगृह्य स्मयासै यदि कण्डूयासै कृष्णविषाणया कण्डूयासै यदि वाचं विसृजेर् वैष्णवीम् ऋचम् अनुद्रवतात् । मा त्वान्यत्र दीक्षितविमितात् सूर्यो ऽभ्युदियात् । माभिनिम्रुक्तात् । यानि देवतानामानि यथाख्यातं तान्य् आचक्ष्वाथ यान्य् अदेवतानामानि यथाख्यातं तान्य् आचक्षाण उपरिष्टाद् विचक्षणं धेहि चनसितवतीं विचक्षणवतीं वाचं वद कृष्णाजिनान् मा व्यवच्छेत्था दण्डाच् च । इति
6.6.162.m: 'You are consecrated. Speak speech suitable for one consecrated. Speak only truth, not untruth. Do not smile. Do not scratch yourself. Do not uncover yourself. If you smile, smile having covered [your mouth]. If you scratch yourself, scratch with the black antelope horn. If you release speech, recite after it a verse to Viṣṇu. Let not the sun rise upon you anywhere outside the shed of the consecrated. Let it not set [upon you]. What are names of deities, speak them as they are known; but what are names of non-deities, speaking them as they are known, add the word vicakṣaṇa at the end. Speak gracious speech, accompanied by vicakṣaṇa. Do not separate from the black antelope skin and from the staff.'
He does all this in just this manner.

6.6.162.s: athopasamindhanavelāyām uttareṇāhavanīyaṃ tiṣṭhan saṃpraiṣam āha | agnīñ jyotiṣmataḥ kuruta dīkṣita vācaṃ yaccha patni vācaṃ yaccha | iti
6.6.162.d: अथोपसमिन्धनवेलायाम् उत्तरेणाहवनीयं तिष्ठन् संप्रैषम् आह । अग्नीञ् ज्योतिष्मतः कुरुत दीक्षित वाचं यच्छ पत्नि वाचं यच्छ । इति
6.6.162.m: Then, at the time of kindling the fires, standing to the north of the āhavanīya fire, he utters the direction: 'Make the fires bright with light! Consecrated one, keep silence! Wife, keep silence!'

6.6.162.s: saṃpreṣya vācaṃyamayor vrate dohayatas | athādhvaryuḥ pūrvayā dvāropaniṣkramya dohayitvaitenaiva yathetam etya gārhapatye 'gnihotravidhiṃ ceṣṭitvā taptvodag udvāsya śītīkṛtvātacya vānātacya vottare śālākhaṇḍe śikya āsajati |
6.6.162.d: संप्रेष्य वाचंयमयोर् व्रते दोहयतस् । अथाध्वर्युः पूर्वया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य दोहयित्वैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्य गार्हपत्ये ऽग्निहोत्रविधिं चेष्टित्वा तप्त्वोदग् उद्वास्य शीतीकृत्वातच्य वानातच्य वोत्तरे शालाखण्डे शिक्य आसजति ।
6.6.162.m: Having issued the direction, while the two are keeping silence, they milk the fast-milks. Then the adhvaryu priest, having stepped out by the eastern door, having had [the cow] milked, having returned by the very way he went, having performed the procedure of the agnihotra at the gārhapatya fire, having heated it, having removed it towards the north, having cooled it, having curdled it or without curdling it, hangs it in a swing-basket in the northern part of the shed.

6.6.162.s: atha pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇayā dvāropaniṣkramya dohayitvaitenaiva yathetam etya vrataśrapaṇe taptvodag udvāsya śītīkṛtvātacya vānātacya vā dakṣiṇe śālākhaṇḍe śikya āsajati |
6.6.162.d: अथ प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्य दोहयित्वैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्य व्रतश्रपणे तप्त्वोदग् उद्वास्य शीतीकृत्वातच्य वानातच्य वा दक्षिणे शालाखण्डे शिक्य आसजति ।
6.6.162.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ priest, having stepped out by the southern door, having had [the cow] milked, having returned by the very way he went, having heated it at the fast-food-cooking hearth, having removed it towards the north, having cooled it, having curdled it or without curdling it, hangs it in a swing-basket in the southern part of the shed.

6.6.163.s: athoditeṣu nakṣatreṣu yajamānaḥ kṛṣṇājinam āsajya pūrvayā dvāropaniṣkramyāgreṇa śālāṃ tiṣṭhan bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar vrataṃ kṛṇuta vrataṃ kṛṇuta | iti trir vācaṃ visṛjate |
6.6.163.d: अथोदितेषु नक्षत्रेषु यजमानः कृष्णाजिनम् आसज्य पूर्वया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्याग्रेण शालां तिष्ठन् भूर् भुवः सुवर् व्रतं कृणुत व्रतं कृणुत । इति त्रिर् वाचं विसृजते ।
6.6.163.m: Then, when the stars have risen, the sacrificer, having put on the black antelope skin, having stepped out by the eastern door, standing in front of the shed, releases his speech three times: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar! Prepare the fast-food! Prepare the fast-food!'

6.6.163.s: athātithīnām upasthām eti canasitavatīṃ vicakṣaṇavatīṃ vācaṃ vadati
6.6.163.d: अथातिथीनाम् उपस्थाम् एति चनसितवतीं विचक्षणवतीं वाचं वदति
6.6.163.m: Then he approaches the guests. He speaks gracious speech, accompanied by vicakṣaṇa.

6.6.163.s: sa yady u hāmedhyam upādhigacchati taj japati | abaddhaṃ mano daridraṃ cakṣuḥ sūryo jyotiṣām̐ śreṣṭho dīkṣe mā mā hāsīs | iti |
6.6.163.d: स यद्य् उ हामेध्यम् उपाधिगच्छति तज् जपति । अबद्धं मनो दरिद्रं चक्षुः सूर्यो ज्योतिषाँ श्रेष्ठो दीक्षे मा मा हासीस् । इति ।
6.6.163.m: If he happens to encounter something impure, he mutters this: 'Unbound is the mind, poor is the eye; the sun is best of lights. O consecration, do not abandon me!'

6.6.163.s: atha yady enam abhivarṣati | undatīr balaṃ dhattaujo dhatta balaṃ dhatta ma me dīkṣāṃ mā tapo nirvadhiṣṭa | ity evaṃ tatra japati
6.6.163.d: अथ यद्य् एनम् अभिवर्षति । उन्दतीर् बलं धत्तौजो धत्त बलं धत्त म मे दीक्षां मा तपो निर्वधिष्ट । इत्य् एवं तत्र जपति
6.6.163.m: Then, if it rains upon him, he then mutters thus: 'O wetting waters, give strength, give vigour, give strength! Do not strike down my consecration, nor my ascetic heat!'

6.6.163.s: tasyaite yajuṣī pariplave ā sam̐sthāyai bhavatas |
6.6.163.d: तस्यैते यजुषी परिप्लवे आ सँस्थायै भवतस् ।
6.6.163.m: These two yajus formulas of his are recurrent until the conclusion [of the sacrifice].

6.6.163.s: athāsmai nipataḥ kāle yajamānāyatane kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti
6.6.163.d: अथास्मै निपतः काले यजमानायतने कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति
6.6.163.m: Then, at the time of lying down, he spreads for him the black antelope skin in the place of the sacrificer, with its neck to the east and the hairy side turned up.

6.6.163.s: sa yadi bahutayam upastīrṇaṃ bhavati kṛṣṇājinād evānantarhitaḥ saṃviśati |
6.6.163.d: स यदि बहुतयम् उपस्तीर्णं भवति कृष्णाजिनाद् एवानन्तर्हितः संविशति ।
6.6.163.m: If many [layers] are spread out, he lies down without being separated from the black antelope skin itself.
Then he mutters the lying-down yajus:

6.7.163.s: agne tvam̐ su jāgṛhi vayam̐ su mandiṣīmahi | gopāya naḥ svastaye prabudhe naḥ punar dadas | iti
6.7.163.d: अग्ने त्वँ सु जागृहि वयँ सु मन्दिषीमहि । गोपाय नः स्वस्तये प्रबुधे नः पुनर् ददस् । इति
6.7.163.m: 'O Agni, keep good watch! May we rejoice well! / Guard us for well-being; give us back for waking!'

6.7.163.s: dakṣiṇataḥ śaya etad vai yajamānasyāyatanam̐ sva evāyatane śaye 'gnim abhyāvṛtya śaye devatā eva yajñam abhyāvṛtya śaye | iti brāhmaṇam
6.7.163.d: दक्षिणतः शय एतद् वै यजमानस्यायतनँ स्व एवायतने शये ऽग्निम् अभ्यावृत्य शये देवता एव यज्ञम् अभ्यावृत्य शये । इति ब्राह्मणम्
6.7.163.m: 'He lies to the south; this indeed is the sacrificer's place; he lies in his own place; he lies turned towards the fire; he lies turned towards the deities, towards the sacrifice,' says the brāhmaṇa passage.

6.7.163.s: athaiṣā patnī jaghanena gārhapatyam̐ saṃviśati tūṣṇīm
6.7.163.d: अथैषा पत्नी जघनेन गार्हपत्यँ संविशति तूष्णीम्
6.7.163.m: Then this wife lies down behind the gārhapatya fire silently.

6.7.163.s: athādhvaryur madhyarātra ādrutya prabuddhayajur vācayati tvam agne vratapā asi deva ā martyeṣv ā | tvaṃ yajñeṣv īḍyas | iti |
6.7.163.d: अथाध्वर्युर् मध्यरात्र आद्रुत्य प्रबुद्धयजुर् वाचयति त्वम् अग्ने व्रतपा असि देव आ मर्त्येष्व् आ । त्वं यज्ञेष्व् ईड्यस् । इति ।
6.7.163.m: Then the adhvaryu priest, having hastened up at midnight, makes him recite the waking yajus: 'You, Agni, are the protector of the vow, / a god among mortals! / You are to be praised at the sacrifices!'

6.7.163.s: athāpa ācāmati daivīṃ dhiyaṃ manāmahe sumṛḍīkām abhiṣṭaye | varcodhām yajñavāhasam | supārā no asad vaśe | iti |
6.7.163.d: अथाप आचामति दैवीं धियं मनामहे सुमृडीकाम् अभिष्टये । वर्चोधाम् यज्ञवाहसम् । सुपारा नो असद् वशे । इति ।
6.7.163.m: Then he sips water [with the verse]: 'We contemplate the divine thought, / very gracious for our assistance, / bringing splendor, conveying the sacrifice. / May it be easy to cross under our control!'

6.7.164.s: athāsmai kam̐se vā camase vā niḥṣicya vrataṃ prayacchati
6.7.164.d: अथास्मै कँसे वा चमसे वा निःषिच्य व्रतं प्रयच्छति
6.7.164.m: Then, having poured out [the fast-milk] into a bronze vessel or into a wooden cup, he offers him the fast-milk.

6.7.164.s: tad dakṣiṇataḥ pariśritya vratayati ye devā manojātā manoyujaḥ sudakṣā dakṣapitāras te naḥ pāntu te no 'vantu tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā | iti |
6.7.164.d: तद् दक्षिणतः परिश्रित्य व्रतयति ये देवा मनोजाता मनोयुजः सुदक्षा दक्षपितारस् ते नः पान्तु ते नो ऽवन्तु तेभ्यो नमस् तेभ्यः स्वाहा । इति ।
6.7.164.m: Having screened him on the south, he consumes the fast-milk [with the formula]: 'Whichever gods are mind-born, mind-yoked, very skillful, whose father is skill, may they protect us! May they help us! Homage to them! Svāhā to them!'

6.7.164.s: yajuṣā yāvanmātraṃ vratayitvā tūṣṇīṃ bhūyo vratayati | etasmin kāle pratiprasthātā patnyai pātre niḥṣicya vrataṃ prayacchati
6.7.164.d: यजुषा यावन्मात्रं व्रतयित्वा तूष्णीं भूयो व्रतयति । एतस्मिन् काले प्रतिप्रस्थाता पत्न्यै पात्रे निःषिच्य व्रतं प्रयच्छति
6.7.164.m: Having consumed as much as is [prescribed] with the yajus, he consumes more silently. At this time the pratiprasthātṛ priest, having poured out [the fast-milk] into a vessel for the wife, offers her the fast-milk.

6.7.164.s: tat sā pariśritya vratayati tūṣṇīm | nirṇijya pātre prayacchatas |
6.7.164.d: तत् सा परिश्रित्य व्रतयति तूष्णीम् । निर्णिज्य पात्रे प्रयच्छतस् ।
6.7.164.m: Having screened her, she consumes it silently. Having washed them, the two return the vessels.

6.7.164.s: atha tathaiva purā nakṣatrāṇām antardhānāt saṃpreṣya vācaṃyamayor vrate dohayatas |
6.7.164.d: अथ तथैव पुरा नक्षत्राणाम् अन्तर्धानात् संप्रेष्य वाचंयमयोर् व्रते दोहयतस् ।
6.7.164.m: Then, in the same way, before the disappearance of the stars, having issued the direction, while the two are keeping silence, they milk the fast-milks.

6.7.164.s: athodita āditye yajamānaḥ kṛṣṇājinam āsajya pūrvayā dvāropaniṣkramyāgreṇa śālāṃ tiṣṭhan bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar vrataṃ kṛṇuta vrataṃ kṛṇuta | iti trir vācaṃ visṛjate
6.7.164.d: अथोदित आदित्ये यजमानः कृष्णाजिनम् आसज्य पूर्वया द्वारोपनिष्क्रम्याग्रेण शालां तिष्ठन् भूर् भुवः सुवर् व्रतं कृणुत व्रतं कृणुत । इति त्रिर् वाचं विसृजते
6.7.164.m: Then, when the sun has risen, the sacrificer, having put on the black antelope skin, having stepped out by the eastern door, standing in front of the shed, releases his speech three times: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar! Prepare the fast-food! Prepare the fast-food!'

6.7.164.s: samāno vāco visargaḥ samānam̐ saṃveśanayajuḥ samānaṃ prabuddhayajuḥ samānam apām ācamanam̐ samānaṃ vratanam
6.7.164.d: समानो वाचो विसर्गः समानँ संवेशनयजुः समानं प्रबुद्धयजुः समानम् अपाम् आचमनँ समानं व्रतनम्
6.7.164.m: Identical is the release of speech; identical is the lying-down yajus; identical is the waking yajus; identical is the sipping of water; identical is the consuming of the fast-milk.

6.7.164.s: atha sanīhārān prahiṇoti sa yaṃ manyate na mā pratyākhyāsyatīti taṃ prathamam abhi prahiṇoti viśve devā abhi mām āvavṛtran pūṣā sanyā somo rādhasā devaḥ savitā vasor vasudāvā | iti |
6.7.164.d: अथ सनीहारान् प्रहिणोति स यं मन्यते न मा प्रत्याख्यास्यतीति तं प्रथमम् अभि प्रहिणोति विश्वे देवा अभि माम् आववृत्रन् पूषा सन्या सोमो राधसा देवः सविता वसोर् वसुदावा । इति ।
6.7.164.m: Then he sends out seekers of gifts. He sends first towards him whom he thinks: 'He will not refuse me,' [with the formula]: 'May the All-gods turn towards me, Pūṣan with gain, Soma with bounty, the divine Savitar, giver of wealth, with wealth!'

6.7.164.s: āharantaṃ dṛṣṭvā japati nānāharantam | rāsveyat soma | ā bhūyo bhara mā pṛṇan pūrtyā virādhi māham āyuṣā | iti
6.7.164.d: आहरन्तं दृष्ट्वा जपति नानाहरन्तम् । रास्वेयत् सोम । आ भूयो भर मा पृणन् पूर्त्या विराधि माहम् आयुषा । इति
6.7.164.m: Seeing one who brings, he mutters, not one who does not bring: 'Grant so much, O Soma! Bring more! May the giver not fail through fulfillment; may I not through life!'
He accepts [the gift] according to its form:

6.8.164.s: candram asi | iti hiraṇyam | vastram asi | iti vāsas | usrāsi | iti gām |
6.8.164.d: चन्द्रम् असि । इति हिरण्यम् । वस्त्रम् असि । इति वासस् । उस्रासि । इति गाम् ।
6.8.164.m: 'You are shining,' [he accepts] gold. 'You are a garment,' clothing. 'You are a reddish cow,' a cow.

6.8.164.s: hayo 'si | ity aśvam | chāgo 'si | iti chāgam | meṣo 'si | iti meṣam atha yad brāhmaṇenānādiṣṭaṃ bhavati prājāpatyam asi mama bhogāya bhava | ity eva tat pratigṛhṇāti
6.8.164.d: हयो ऽसि । इत्य् अश्वम् । छागो ऽसि । इति छागम् । मेषो ऽसि । इति मेषम् अथ यद् ब्राह्मणेनानादिष्टं भवति प्राजापत्यम् असि मम भोगाय भव । इत्य् एव तत् प्रतिगृह्णाति
6.8.164.m: 'You are a horse,' a horse. 'You are a he-goat,' a he-goat. 'You are a ram,' a ram. And what has not been indicated by the brāhmaṇa passage, he accepts only with: 'You belong to Prajāpati; be for my enjoyment!'

6.8.164.s: tāḥ samudāyutya rakṣanti tāsāṃ yā naśyati vā mriyate vā vāyave tvā | iti tām anudiśati
6.8.164.d: ताः समुदायुत्य रक्षन्ति तासां या नश्यति वा म्रियते वा वायवे त्वा । इति ताम् अनुदिशति
6.8.164.m: Having gathered them together, they guard them. Whichever of them is lost or dies, he assigns it with: 'To Vāyu you!'

6.8.165.s: yāpsu vā pāśe vā varuṇāya tvā | iti tām |
6.8.165.d: याप्सु वा पाशे वा वरुणाय त्वा । इति ताम् ।
6.8.165.m: Whichever [perishes] in the water or in a snare, [he assigns] it with: 'To Varuṇa you!'

6.8.165.s: yā saṃ vā śīryate gartaṃ vā patati nirṛtyai tvā | iti tām |
6.8.165.d: या सं वा शीर्यते गर्तं वा पतति निरृत्यै त्वा । इति ताम् ।
6.8.165.m: Whichever breaks to pieces or falls into a pit, [he assigns] it with: 'To Nirṛti you!'

6.8.165.s: yāmahir vā vyāghro vā hanti rudrāya tvā | iti tām | tāsāṃ tisraḥ parācyas |
6.8.165.d: यामहिर् वा व्याघ्रो वा हन्ति रुद्राय त्वा । इति ताम् । तासां तिस्रः पराच्यस् ।
6.8.165.m: Whichever a snake or a tiger kills, [he assigns] it with: 'To Rudra you!' Three of them are turned away.

6.8.165.s: atha yeyaṃ naṣṭā yadi vindeyuḥ katham̐ syād iti |
6.8.165.d: अथ येयं नष्टा यदि विन्देयुः कथँ स्याद् इति ।
6.8.165.m: Now, as to this [cow] that was lost, if they should find it, what would happen?

6.8.165.s: etad anudiṣṭaiva syād ity etad ekam | kam asyā ataḥ śreyām̐saṃ pratigrahītāraṃ labheta
6.8.165.d: एतद् अनुदिष्टैव स्याद् इत्य् एतद् एकम् । कम् अस्या अतः श्रेयाँसं प्रतिग्रहीतारं लभेत
6.8.165.m: 'It should remain just as assigned'—this is one view. 'What better recipient than this could one find for it?'

6.8.165.s: dakṣiṇābhir evainām̐ saha dadyād ity ekam |
6.8.165.d: दक्षिणाभिर् एवैनाँ सह दद्याद् इत्य् एकम् ।
6.8.165.m: "He should give her along with the priestly gifts," is one [view].
"He should sacrifice with her to Vāyu," is another [view].

6.9.165.s: athātaḥ prayāṇasyaiva mīmām̐sā dīkṣtitaṃ vāyogakṣemo vindaty anyatra vā devayajanād dīkṣate sam̐sṛjanti vrate
6.9.165.d: अथातः प्रयाणस्यैव मीमाँसा दीक्ष्तितं वायोगक्षेमो विन्दत्य् अन्यत्र वा देवयजनाद् दीक्षते सँसृजन्ति व्रते
6.9.165.m:
Now follows the investigation of setting forth [on a journey]:
either anxiety regarding livelihood overtakes the consecrated [sacrificer], or he is consecrated elsewhere than at the sacrificial place. They blend the fast-milk [oblations].
They tie up the two calves of the two fast-milk cows.

6.9.165.s: ādadhati yadāgheyaṃ bhavati nīḍe gārhapatyaṃ prauga āhavanīyam
6.9.165.d: आदधति यदाघेयं भवति नीडे गार्हपत्यं प्रौग आहवनीयम्
6.9.165.m: They put [into the cart] whatever is to be placed: the gārhapatya [fire] in the seat [of the cart], the āhavanīya [fire] in the cart-pole.

6.9.165.s: api vāraṇyor agnīn samārohya bṛhaspativatyarcā prayāti bhadrād abhi śreyaḥ prehi bṛhaspatiḥ puraetā te astu | iti |
6.9.165.d: अपि वारण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य बृहस्पतिवत्यर्चा प्रयाति भद्राद् अभि श्रेयः प्रेहि बृहस्पतिः पुरएता ते अस्तु । इति ।
6.9.165.m: Or, having mounted the fires into the two churning sticks, he sets forth with the verse containing [the name of] Bṛhaspati: "Go forth from good to better! Let Bṛhaspati be your guide!"

6.9.165.s: atha yady enaṃ yāntaṃ vratanavelopādhigacchaty uttarato 'raṇī nidhāya dakṣiṇataḥ pariśritya vratayati
6.9.165.d: अथ यद्य् एनं यान्तं व्रतनवेलोपाधिगच्छत्य् उत्तरतो ऽरणी निधाय दक्षिणतः परिश्रित्य व्रतयति
6.9.165.m: Then, if the time for the fast-milk reaches him while he is travelling, having placed the two churning sticks to the north, having enclosed [the space] to the south, he consumes the fast-milk.

6.9.165.s: tūṣṇīṃ tṛṇodakāyāvasyati | atha yady aparyāṇā apa upādhigacchati taj japati devīr āpo apāṃ napād ya ūrmir haviṣya indriyāvān madintamas taṃ vo māvakramiṣam acchinnaṃ tantuṃ pṛthivyā anu geṣam iti
6.9.165.d: तूष्णीं तृणोदकायावस्यति । अथ यद्य् अपर्याणा अप उपाधिगच्छति तज् जपति देवीर् आपो अपां नपाद् य ऊर्मिर् हविष्य इन्द्रियावान् मदिन्तमस् तं वो मावक्रमिषम् अच्छिन्नं तन्तुं पृथिव्या अनु गेषम् इति
6.9.165.m: Silently he halts for grass and water. Then, if he encounters waters that cannot be driven through around, he mutters that [mantra]: "Divine waters, Son of the Waters! Whatever wave of yours is fit for oblation, powerful, most exhilarating, let me not step down upon that of yours! May I pursue the unbroken thread of the earth!"

6.9.166.s: saṃ vā gāhate saṃ vā tarati
6.9.166.d: सं वा गाहते सं वा तरति
6.9.166.m: He plunges in or crosses over.
"He crosses over making indeed a bridge," says a brāhmaṇa passage.

6.9.166.s: athādityam udyantam upatiṣṭhate | āre śatrūn kṛṇuhi sarvavīras | iti |
6.9.166.d: अथादित्यम् उद्यन्तम् उपतिष्ठते । आरे शत्रून् कृणुहि सर्ववीरस् । इति ।
6.9.166.m: Then he waits upon the rising sun with: "Drive the enemies far away, with all our heroes!"

6.9.166.s: atha yatra yakṣyamāṇo bhavati tad avasyati | edam aganma devayajanaṃ pṛthivyās | ity āntād anuvākasya ||
6.9.166.d: अथ यत्र यक्ष्यमाणो भवति तद् अवस्यति । एदम् अगन्म देवयजनं पृथिव्यास् । इत्य् आन्ताद् अनुवाकस्य ॥
6.9.166.m: Then, where he is going to sacrifice, there he settles with: "Here have we come to the sacrificial place of the earth!" to the end of the section.

6.10.166.s: athātaḥ krayasyaivopavasathaḥ paryāplavate sa upakalpayate candraṃ ca chāgāṃ ca kṛṣṇabalakṣyāv ūrṇāstuke uṣṇīṣaṃ dve vāsasī dve kṛṣṇājine somakrayaṇīm̐ saiṣāruṇā piṅgalaikahāyanī bhavati somavāhanāv anaḍvāhau somavāhanam anaḥ prakṣālitam uddhṛtaphalakam̐ rohitaṃ carmānaḍuhaṃ dvayam idhmābarhiḥ kārṣmaryamayān paridhīn āśvavālaṃ prastaram aikṣavī vidhṛtī sthālīṃ paddharaṇīm am̐śugrahaṇam̐ hiraṇyam audumbarīm̐ rājāsandīṃ tasyai nābhidaghnāḥ pādā bhavanty aratnimātrāṇi śīrṣāṇy anūcyāni
6.10.166.d: अथातः क्रयस्यैवोपवसथः पर्याप्लवते स उपकल्पयते चन्द्रं च छागां च कृष्णबलक्ष्याव् ऊर्णास्तुके उष्णीषं द्वे वाससी द्वे कृष्णाजिने सोमक्रयणीँ सैषारुणा पिङ्गलैकहायनी भवति सोमवाहनाव् अनड्वाहौ सोमवाहनम् अनः प्रक्षालितम् उद्धृतफलकँ रोहितं चर्मानडुहं द्वयम् इध्माबर्हिः कार्ष्मर्यमयान् परिधीन् आश्ववालं प्रस्तरम् ऐक्षवी विधृती स्थालीं पद्धरणीम् अँशुग्रहणँ हिरण्यम् औदुम्बरीँ राजासन्दीं तस्यै नाभिदघ्नाः पादा भवन्त्य् अरत्निमात्राणि शीर्षाण्य् अनूच्यानि
6.10.166.m:
Now follows the fast-day of the purchase [of soma], which comes around.
He procures: gold, a she-goat, two tufts of wool, one black and one white, a turban, two cloths, two black antelope skins, the soma-purchasing cow—and she is reddish-brown, yellow-eyed, and one year old—two draft-oxen to carry the soma, a cart to carry the soma, washed and with its boards removed, a red ox-hide, two sets of kindling wood and sacrificial grass, enclosing sticks of kārṣmarya wood, a grass bundle of horse-tail grass, two reed separators, a pot, an earthen plate, a vessel for collecting the shoots, a piece of gold, and a king's stool of udumbara wood. Its legs are navel-high, its head-pieces and side-pieces are a cubit long.

6.10.166.s: sā mauñjībhī rajjubhir vyūtā bhavaty ekasarābhis |
6.10.166.d: सा मौञ्जीभी रज्जुभिर् व्यूता भवत्य् एकसराभिस् ।
6.10.166.m: It is interwoven with cords of muñja grass, consisting of single strands.

6.10.166.s: manāgvarṣīyasīm iva samrāḍāsandīṃ yadi pravargyavān somo bhavati |
6.10.166.d: मनाग्वर्षीयसीम् इव सम्राडासन्दीं यदि प्रवर्ग्यवान् सोमो भवति ।
6.10.166.m: A slightly larger sovereign stool [is prepared] if the soma [sacrifice] is accompanied by the pravargya.

6.10.166.s: athādhvaryur apararātra ādrutya sam̐śāsti tristanavrataṃ dohayata | iti
6.10.166.d: अथाध्वर्युर् अपररात्र आद्रुत्य सँशास्ति त्रिस्तनव्रतं दोहयत । इति
6.10.166.m: Then the adhvaryu priest, running up in the latter part of the night, gives instructions: "Milk the fast-milk of three teats!"

6.10.167.s: prātarudita āditye visṛṣṭāyāṃ vācy agreṇa śālāṃ tiṣṭhan devayajanam adhyavasyati yadi purastād anadhyavasitaṃ bhavati |
6.10.167.d: प्रातरुदित आदित्ये विसृष्टायां वाच्य् अग्रेण शालां तिष्ठन् देवयजनम् अध्यवस्यति यदि पुरस्ताद् अनध्यवसितं भवति ।
6.10.167.m: In the morning, when the sun has risen, when speech has been released, standing in front of the hall, he settles upon the sacrificial ground, if it has not been settled upon beforehand.

6.10.167.s: pūrvayā dvārā śālāṃ prapādya pṛṣṭhyām̐ stīrtvāpaḥ praṇīyādityaṃ carum prāyaṇīyām iṣṭiṃ nirvapati
6.10.167.d: पूर्वया द्वारा शालां प्रपाद्य पृष्ठ्याँ स्तीर्त्वापः प्रणीयादित्यं चरुम् प्रायणीयाम् इष्टिं निर्वपति
6.10.167.m: Having made him enter the hall by the eastern door, having spread the line of the spine, having led forth the waters, he measures out the boiled rice for Aditi for the introductory offering.

6.10.167.s: haviṣkṛtā vācaṃ visṛjya gārhapatya ājyaṃ vilāpyotpūyāhavanīye sruvāhutiṃ juhoti kavir yajñasya vitanoti panthāṃ nākasya pṛṣṭhe adhi rocane divaḥ | yena havyaṃ vahasi yāsi dūta itaḥ pracetā amutaḥ sanīyān svāhā | iti |
6.10.167.d: हविष्कृता वाचं विसृज्य गार्हपत्य आज्यं विलाप्योत्पूयाहवनीये स्रुवाहुतिं जुहोति कविर् यज्ञस्य वितनोति पन्थां नाकस्य पृष्ठे अधि रोचने दिवः । येन हव्यं वहसि यासि दूत इतः प्रचेता अमुतः सनीयान् स्वाहा । इति ।
6.10.167.m: Having released speech with the [call to the] preparer of the oblation, having melted the clarified butter on the gārhapatya [fire] and purified it, he offers a ladle libation on the āhavanīya fire with: "The poet extends the path of the sacrifice upon the back of the firmament, upon the brightness of the sky; whereby you carry the oblation, you go as a messenger hence, wise, to win [goods] from yonder, svāhā!"

6.10.167.s: athopaniṣkramya saṃpraiṣam āha somavikrayin somam̐ śodhayoparavāṇāṃ kāle rohite carmaṇy ānaḍuhe 'pāmante brāhmaṇo dakṣiṇata āstāṃ tā gāvo dūraṃ mā guryāsu somakrayaṇī ca somavāhanau cānaḍvāhau somavāhanam anaḥ prakṣālayatoddhṛtaphalakam iti
6.10.167.d: अथोपनिष्क्रम्य संप्रैषम् आह सोमविक्रयिन् सोमँ शोधयोपरवाणां काले रोहिते चर्मण्य् आनडुहे ऽपामन्ते ब्राह्मणो दक्षिणत आस्तां ता गावो दूरं मा गुर्यासु सोमक्रयणी च सोमवाहनौ चानड्वाहौ सोमवाहनम् अनः प्रक्षालयतोद्धृतफलकम् इति
6.10.167.m: Then, having stepped outside, he utters the direction: "Soma-seller, cleanse the soma! At the time of the sound-holes, on the red ox-hide, near the water, let a brāhmaṇa sit to the south. Let those cows not wander far away, among which are the soma-purchasing cow and the two draft-oxen to carry the soma. Wash the cart that carries the soma, with its boards removed!"
